# Pricing and Discount Policy, H2 2026

**Owner:** Priya Kaplan, Head of Pricing and Packaging
**Reviewed by:** Ruth Lindqvist, Chief Financial Officer
**Effective:** July 1, 2026
**Applies to:** All account executives, Customer Success Managers, and Revenue Operations

## Purpose

This document sets the list prices for Northstar Systems products in the second half of 2026 and defines who may approve discounts off list. It replaces the pricing guidance circulated in the first half of the year. Account teams should use it when preparing quotes, renewal proposals, and order forms. Questions go to Pricing and Packaging, and nothing in this document overrides a signed order form.

## List Prices

Every Northstar product is priced per truck per month. No product is sold on a flat platform fee or per-seat basis for H2 2026.

| Product | List price | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| Northstar Track | $14 | per truck per month |
| Predict ETA | $9 | per truck per month |
| Dock Scheduler | $6 | per truck per month |

Quotes should show each product on its own line. Bundles are priced as the sum of the component list prices unless a bundle price has been approved in writing by Pricing and Packaging.

## Counting Trucks

The billable count is the number of trucks active on the account during the billing month, measured as the highest number of trucks reporting in any single day. Trucks that are decommissioned mid-month are billed for the full month. Dock Scheduler is billed on the trucks that have at least one dock appointment booked in the month, unless the contract states otherwise. Revenue Operations will confirm the count from platform data before each invoice run.

## Discount Authority

Discounts are measured as a percentage off the list price of the product line in question. The approval levels are as follows.

**Account executive, up to 10%.** An account executive may apply a discount of up to 10% on their own authority, provided the discount is recorded on the opportunity in the CRM before the quote is sent.

**VP Sales, up to 25%.** Any discount above 10% and up to 25% requires approval from the VP Sales for the region. Requests go through the approval queue in the CRM with a short justification, the competitive or commercial reason, and the expected term. Approval requests should be raised before the price is shared with the customer.

**Chief Financial Officer, above 25%.** Any discount larger than 25% goes to the Chief Financial Officer. These requests also require the VP Sales to sign off first. Ruth Lindqvist reviews them weekly, and urgent requests can be raised directly in the finance channel.

Discounts may not be stacked. A multi-year commitment discount and a volume discount on the same line are measured together against the table above, not added to each other on top of it.

## Multi-Year and Volume Terms

Customers committing to a 24-month term may receive a term discount of up to 8%, which counts toward the total discount on the line. Volume tiers are set by Pricing and Packaging and published in the internal rate card. Account executives should not offer tier pricing that is not in the rate card.

## Non-Standard Terms

Free pilots, extended ramp periods, and credits against implementation work are not discounts for the purposes of this policy, but each must be approved by Pricing and Packaging and recorded on the order form. Pilots longer than 60 days require CFO approval regardless of value.

## Exceptions and Escalation

If a deal does not fit this policy, the account executive should describe the situation to Pricing and Packaging before negotiating further. Do not promise pricing to a customer while an approval is pending. Verbal commitments outside this policy are not binding on Northstar Systems.

## Review

This policy will be reviewed at the end of Q3 2026. Changes to list prices will be announced to account teams at least four weeks before they take effect.

**Key:** TRK-2205
**Type:** Story
**Priority:** High
**Status:** In Progress
**Assignee:** Noa Calloway (Data Engineer)
**Reporter:** Daniel Hernandez (QA Engineer)
**Component:** Northstar Track / Exports
**Labels:** background-jobs, exports, customer-requested
**Created:** July 1, 2026, 10:08 UTC

**Summary:** CSV export as background job

**Description**

**Context**

Customers with large fleets are hitting timeouts when they export shipment and stop history from Northstar Track. The current export runs synchronously in the web request. For accounts with more than about 40,000 stop events in the selected range, the request times out at the load balancer, and the user sees a blank download or a generic error. Support has logged eleven such tickets in the past month, and two of the affected accounts are in the renewal window this quarter.

Moving the export to a background job lets the request return immediately with a job ID. The job writes the file to object storage, and the user gets a notification with a signed download link when it is ready.

**Scope**

- Export requests for shipment history and stop events become queued jobs.
- Completed files are stored for 7 days, then deleted by the existing retention job.
- The Exports page shows job status: queued, running, complete, failed.
- The download link is scoped to the requesting user and expires after 24 hours.

**Out of scope**

- Changes to the CSV column layout. Column order and headers stay as they are today.
- Excel or JSON formats.
- Scheduled recurring exports.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. A request for a range with 200,000 stop events returns a job ID in under 2 seconds.
2. The job completes and the file matches the synchronous export byte-for-byte for a 5,000-row reference dataset.
3. A failed job shows a readable error on the Exports page and can be retried once from the UI.
4. The requesting user receives an email with the download link when the job completes.
5. A user in a different account cannot access the file via a guessed URL (returns 404, not 403).
6. Existing synchronous export still works behind the feature flag `exports_async` until the flag is removed.

**Owner:** Noa Calloway
**Dependencies:** Object storage bucket policy update (owned by the platform team). Email template review by Marketing.

**DOCK-641: Slot length templates**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Key** | DOCK-641 |
| **Type** | Story |
| **Priority** | High |
| **Status** | In Progress |
| **Assignee** | Oskar Jensen (ML Engineer, Northstar Systems) |
| **Reporter** | Oskar Jensen (ML Engineer, Northstar Systems) |
| **Component** | Dock Scheduler / Appointment Booking |
| **Created** | July 1, 2026, 14:26 UTC |

**Description**

*Context*

Dock Scheduler currently asks warehouse admins to type a slot length in minutes every time they create a dock appointment. Customers with repeatable inbound and outbound patterns have told us this is slow and error-prone. A carrier dispatcher at one of our larger accounts booked 45-minute slots for full trailer unloads that actually need 90, and the yard filled up before anyone caught it. Support logged three similar cases last quarter.

Slot length templates let an admin define a named template (for example, "LTL inbound, 60 min" or "Full trailer live unload, 90 min"), attach it to a dock door or a door group, and have new appointments pick up that length by default. The admin can still override the length on an individual booking.

This is the first step toward the template-based scheduling that Product has on the Q4 plan. It does not change how Predict ETA feeds arrival windows into the scheduler. Arrival prediction stays as it is in this ticket.

*Scope*

- Create, edit, archive and delete slot length templates at the account level.
- Assign a default template to a dock door or door group.
- Apply the default template when a booking is created through the UI or the appointments API.
- Show the template name next to the slot length on the dock calendar.

*Out of scope*

- Changes to yard flow logic or trailer dwell calculations.
- Migration of existing bookings. They keep their current lengths.
- Per-carrier templates. That will be a separate ticket.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. An admin with the Scheduler Admin role can create a template with a name (max 40 characters) and a length between 15 and 240 minutes in 15-minute steps.
2. Archiving a template hides it from new bookings but leaves existing bookings unchanged.
3. Deleting a template is blocked if it is the default for any door; the UI lists the affected doors.
4. A new booking on a door with a default template pre-fills that length. The admin can change it, and the override is saved on the booking.
5. The appointments API accepts an optional `slot_template_id`. If omitted and the door has a default, the default applies. If omitted and no default exists, the existing required `slot_minutes` field applies, so current integrations do not break.
6. The dock calendar displays the template name on each booking that used one.
7. Templates are scoped to one account. A user in account A cannot see or apply templates from account B. Verified by an automated test and a manual check.
8. Load test: the calendar view renders in under 800 ms with 500 bookings across 40 doors, which matches our largest current account.

**Owner**

Oskar Jensen. Rafael Navarro is QA lead for this ticket.

**Status**

In Progress. The data model and the API parameter are merged to the feature branch. The admin UI is about 70% done. Acceptance criteria 1 through 5 are covered by tests.

---

**Comments**

**Rafael Navarro** (QA Engineer, Northstar Systems) – 2026-07-01 14:58 UTC

On criterion 3, deleting a default template from the door settings page works, but the calendar still shows the old name for about 20 seconds until the cache refreshes. Filed as a sub-bug under this ticket. Not a blocker, but I'd like it fixed before the beta flag goes on.

**Oskar Jensen** (ML Engineer, Northstar Systems) – 2026-07-01 15:12 UTC
Thanks. That's the cache key missing the template ID. Fix is small; I'll push it today. I also want to double-check the API default behavior against the integration docs before anyone external sees it, since a few customers script bookings and we can't change their results silently.

**Rafael Navarro** (QA Engineer, Northstar Systems) – 2026-07-01 15:31 UTC
Agreed. I'll write a regression case that books with the old `slot_minutes` field only and confirms the length is unchanged. Adding it to the suite now.

**Oskar Jensen** (ML Engineer, Northstar Systems) – 2026-07-01 15:40 UTC
Good. Once the cache fix and the regression case are in, I'll move criteria 6 and 7 to review. Load test for criterion 8 is scheduled for next week on staging.

# Dock Scheduler Admin Guide

**Author:** Lucia Engstrom, Sales Development Representative
**Last updated:** July 1, 2026, 17:25 UTC
**Applies to:** Dock Scheduler (list price $6 per truck per month)

## Purpose

This guide is for warehouse administrators who set up Dock Scheduler for their facilities. It covers three things: configuring receiving hours, setting slot length per door, and defining carrier booking rules. Most setup takes under an hour once you have your door list and carrier roster ready. Sales and Customer Success can walk through this with you on a call if you prefer.

## Before you start

Gather the following:

- A list of every dock door, including any doors reserved for specific freight types such as refrigerated or oversize loads.
- Your standard receiving hours for each day of the week, including any seasonal changes.
- Your typical unload time by freight type. Pallet freight, floor-loaded trailers and parcel cross-dock usually take different times.
- Your carrier list, with any carriers that need priority or restricted access.

You need the Admin role in your Northstar account to change any of these settings. Users with the Dispatcher role can view the schedule but cannot edit it.

## Step 1: Set receiving hours

Go to **Settings > Facility > Receiving hours**. Each day shows an opening time and a closing time. Add a second window if your facility closes for a lunch break or runs a split shift.

Receiving hours control when the scheduler will offer appointments. Slots outside these hours are never shown to carriers, even if a door is technically free. If a holiday closure applies, add it as an exception date rather than editing the weekly pattern, so your regular hours stay intact.

Keep receiving hours accurate. Predict ETA uses them to adjust arrival estimates for trucks that would otherwise arrive outside your open window, so a wrong setting shows up as misleading arrival times across the account.

## Step 2: Set slot length per door

Go to **Settings > Doors**, select a door, and set the **slot length** for that door. Slot length is the amount of time reserved for one appointment. Common values are 30, 45, 60 and 90 minutes.

You can set slot length per door, not only for the whole facility. A door that handles floor-loaded trailers will usually need a longer slot than a door used for parcel cross-dock. If a door is used for mixed freight, pick the length that fits the slowest common job and note this in the door description so dispatchers know why.

Changing slot length does not move existing bookings. The new length applies to appointments created after the change. Existing bookings keep their original times, and the scheduler flags any overlap so you can resolve it manually.

## Step 3: Define carrier booking rules

Go to **Settings > Carriers > Booking rules**. For each carrier or group of carriers, you can set:

- **Booking window:** how far in advance a carrier can book, for example up to 14 days.
- **Maximum bookings per day:** a cap on how many appointments a carrier can hold on one day.
- **Preferred doors:** doors the carrier is steered toward when a choice is available.
- **Restricted doors:** doors the carrier cannot book, for example a door reserved for a single customer's freight.
- **Cancellation notice:** the minimum notice a carrier must give before cancelling without a penalty flag.

Apply the most specific rule that fits. A rule for a named carrier overrides the group rule, and the group rule overrides the facility default.

## Step 4: Test before go-live

Use the **Preview** button to see what a carrier sees when booking. Check that receiving hours appear correctly, that slot lengths match each door, and that restricted doors do not show up. Book one test appointment per door type, then cancel it.

## Common questions

**Why don't I see slots on a day I expected to be open?** Check for an exception date, and confirm the door's slot length fits inside the remaining window.

**Can a carrier exceed the daily maximum?** Not through the carrier portal. Dispatchers can override the cap manually, and the override is logged.

**Who should I contact if something looks wrong?** Open a ticket with Support, or ask your Customer Success Manager to review the setup with you.

**TRK-2208: Backfill positions after ELD gaps**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Key | TRK-2208 |
| Type | Story |
| Priority | High |
| Status | In Progress |
| Assignee | Uma Lombardi |
| Reporter | Camille Colvin |
| Component | Track ingestion, Predict ETA |
| Created | July 3, 2026, 09:07 UTC |

**Description**

**Context**

When a truck's ELD or telematics feed drops for more than a few minutes, Northstar Track shows a straight line between the last known position and the next received one. For customers with dispatch rules tied to geofence entry, this breaks two things: the on-map trail looks wrong, and Predict ETA receives a position history that implies impossible speeds. Dispatchers at several accounts have flagged arrival predictions that jump by 40 minutes after a feed reconnects.

Right now the pipeline has no gap handling. Points are stored as received, and the ETA feature builder treats the time between them as real travel time. We want a backfill step that estimates positions during gaps, marks them as estimated, and gives the ETA model a clean input.

**Proposed approach**

1. Detect gaps where the interval between consecutive points exceeds the configured threshold (default 5 minutes, per tenant).
2. For each gap, interpolate along the road network using the last known speed and heading, constrained by the route geometry when a planned route exists.
3. Write backfilled points with `source = estimated` and a confidence score. Do not overwrite raw ELD points.
4. Expose a flag to Predict ETA so the feature builder can down-weight or exclude estimated segments.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Gaps over 5 minutes are detected within one ingestion cycle of the feed reconnecting.
- Backfilled points are stored separately from raw points and are never returned as raw telemetry in the API.
- Every estimated point carries `source = estimated` and a confidence value between 0 and 1.
- Interpolated positions stay within the planned route corridor when a route exists, and never imply a speed above the configured vehicle maximum.
- Predict ETA feature builder excludes estimated segments by default; a tenant-level setting can include them.
- On the replay set of 200 gap events from last quarter's staging data, median positional error against the later ELD point is under 1.5 km for gaps up to 15 minutes.
- No change in ETA accuracy for trucks with no gaps (regression check on the standard evaluation set).
- Dashboards show gap count and backfill rate per tenant.

**Out of scope**

- Changes to how raw ELD feeds are ingested or retried.
- Dock Scheduler behavior.

---

Filed this after the Halvorsen Freight Group escalation. Their dispatch team (Ingrid Solberg's group) sees ETA swings every time a truck goes through a dead zone. Uma, can you take the ingestion side first? I'll own the feature builder change and the evaluation set.

# SLA definitions

**Owner:** Kalani Edqvist, Staff Engineer
**Last updated:** July 3, 2026
**Status:** Draft for internal review

## Purpose

This document defines the standard service level agreement (SLA) that Northstar Systems offers to customers on Northstar Track and Dock Scheduler. It sets out how availability is measured, what counts as downtime, and how service credits are issued. Customer-facing language lives in the order form template. This page is the internal reference that Support, Customer Success, and Sales should use when answering questions about commitments.

Predict ETA is not covered by the standard SLA in this version. Predictions are served from the same platform, but accuracy and model refresh schedules are handled under separate product terms.

## Standard commitment

For Track and Dock Scheduler, Northstar commits to 99.9% monthly uptime for the production environment. Uptime is measured per calendar month in UTC and applies to the core services a customer uses daily: ingestion of telematics and ELD feeds, live position updates, appointment booking, and yard flow views.

If monthly uptime falls below the 99.9% commitment, the affected customer is eligible for service credits. Credits are applied to the next invoice for the product that was affected. They are not paid out in cash unless the order form says otherwise.

## What counts as downtime

Downtime is any period where a core service returns errors for more than half of requests from a customer's authenticated sessions, or where live position updates for a customer's fleet are not delivered for longer than the allowed staleness window. The staleness window is defined in the telemetry runbook and is currently fifteen minutes.

The following do not count as downtime:

- Scheduled maintenance announced at least five business days in advance through the status page.
- Failures caused by the customer's own telematics provider, ELD hardware, or network connectivity at the depot.
- Issues in third-party mapping or routing data that Northstar does not control, provided the platform surfaces a clear degraded-mode notice.
- Requests blocked by customer-configured IP restrictions or expired credentials.
- Beta features explicitly marked as excluded from the SLA.

Support should record the start and end time of every incident in the incident log, including the customer-visible impact, so that uptime can be calculated accurately at month end.

## How uptime is calculated

Monthly uptime equals total minutes in the month minus minutes of qualifying downtime, divided by total minutes in the month. Partial incidents are counted proportionally to the share of affected tenants or affected services, using the rules in the incident scoring guide. Finance reviews the calculation before any credit is confirmed.

Where a customer disputes the calculation, Customer Success opens a review with Support Tier 2 and an engineering owner. The review should be completed within the normal billing cycle.

## Service credits

Service credits are a fixed percentage of the monthly fee for the affected product, scaled to how far uptime fell below the 99.9% commitment. The exact credit schedule is maintained by Priya Kaplan's pricing team and is included in the approved order form template. Sales should not offer alternative credit terms without a pricing review.

Credits are the customer's sole remedy for missing the uptime commitment, unless the contract states otherwise. Customers must request credits within the period defined in the order form.

## Responsibilities

- **Engineering** owns uptime monitoring, the incident log, and the monthly availability report.
- **Support** owns customer communication during incidents and the dispute workflow.
- **Finance** confirms credit amounts before they are applied.
- **Customer Success** explains the SLA during onboarding and at renewal.

## Open items

- Confirm whether the staleness window should differ for Dock Scheduler, which updates less frequently than Track.
- Decide whether Predict ETA should receive a separate availability target next quarter.
- Update the status page template so that degraded-mode notices are classified consistently with this document.

**Description**

Coldharbour Transport (furniture delivery, US Midwest, 710 trucks, Northstar Track and Predict ETA) reported through NS-4139 that the CSV export from the Shipments view returns incomplete data for their fleet. Their dispatch team uses the export each morning to reconcile overnight deliveries against their billing system. Two mornings in a row, the file has been missing stops for trucks in the second half of the fleet's ID range, and the Predict ETA columns are blank for some rows.

Support has confirmed the problem is reproducible on the account and is not caused by the customer's filters. The customer has put their monthly renewal conversation on hold until this is resolved, so this is treated as a P1.

**Reproduction steps**

1. Log in to a staging tenant with at least 700 active trucks and Predict ETA enabled.
2. Open Shipments, set the date range to the previous 24 hours, and select all trucks.
3. Click Export CSV.
4. Count rows in the file and compare against the Shipments grid total.
5. Observe that the file contains exactly 10,000 rows, while the grid shows 14,212 stops.
6. Open the rows at the end of the file. The ETA columns are empty for stops created after the first 10,000 in the query order.

**Working hypothesis**

The export job pages through results using a cursor on `stop_id` but sorts by `scheduled_at`. When the sort and cursor disagree, the job terminates early after the page limit and reports success. The ETA join is applied after truncation, so late-page rows lose their predictions.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Export row count equals the Shipments grid total for the same filter, verified on a tenant with at least 14,000 stops in range.
- Export cursor and sort key are consistent; a unit test covers paging across more than three pages.
- Predict ETA columns are populated for every row where a prediction exists.
- If the export would exceed the configured limit, the job fails with a visible error and does not return a partial file.
- Customer account NS-4139 re-run confirmed by Support before closing.

**Estimate**

3 story points (about 2 days). Includes the fix, tests, and a backfill check on the Coldharbour Transport tenant.

I looked at the job logs for the customer tenant. The truncation happens at exactly 10,000 rows on both mornings, so this is not a timeout. Uma, you're the right owner since you wrote the paging change in the spring. Please start with the cursor/sort mismatch before touching the ETA join.

**Uma Medina** (July 5, 19:48 UTC)
Confirmed locally. The cursor is built on `stop_id` but the query orders by `scheduled_at`, so page two starts from the wrong position and the loop exits when it gets an empty page. I'll put up a fix behind a flag so we can compare outputs against the grid before we turn it on for Coldharbour. Estimate holds at 3 points.

Summary: DOCK-644: Follow-up: slot length templates

Description:

Follow-up from the Dock Scheduler discovery work last quarter. Warehouse customers currently have to enter appointment slot lengths by hand for every dock door, and several accounts have asked for a way to save a standard set of lengths and reuse it across doors and sites. Today a dispatcher who books a 45-minute live unload at one door and a 90-minute drop-and-hook at another has to create each slot separately, which slows setup and causes mismatches in yard flow reports.

Scope for this ticket:
- Let admins create named slot length templates (for example, "Live unload 45 min" or "Drop and hook 90 min").
- Allow a template to be applied to one or more dock doors in a single action.
- Show the template name on each appointment so dispatch can tell at a glance which rule was used.

Out of scope: changes to ETA-driven slot shifting. That work sits with Predict ETA and is tracked separately.

Acceptance criteria:
1. An admin can create, rename, and delete a template without affecting existing appointments.
2. Applying a template to multiple doors creates or updates slots on each door and reports any conflicts.
3. Appointments created from a template keep a reference to it.
4. Existing hand-entered slots continue to work unchanged.

[10:17] Noa Calloway: Following up on yesterday's page. Webhook delivery p95 is still sitting around 4.8s vs our 1s target. Customer-facing impact is limited to the ETA push webhooks for two fleets, but the latency is spreading. Writing up the timeline in the incident doc now. :thread:

[10:19] Elif Petrakis: Thanks Noa. Before we go further, can we confirm whether this is the same root cause as the June retry storm or something new? I don't want us chasing the wrong thing.

[10:21] Noa Calloway: Different signature. June was retries piling up on the dispatcher. This time the dispatcher queue depth is flat. The delay is between the prediction service publishing and the webhook worker picking it up.

[10:23] Astrid Romero: That lines up with what I saw in the model-serving logs. We rolled the new batch-scoring config on Monday, and it changed how we chunk the output. Chunks are bigger now, so the publisher holds messages longer before flushing. 🤔

[10:25] Noa Calloway: So the publish step is batching more aggressively and the consumer is waiting on bigger payloads. Is that the whole story or are we also seeing slow serialization?

[10:27] Astrid Romero: Serialization is fine, I profiled it. The flush interval is the culprit. We set it to 2s thinking it would reduce broker chatter. Should have checked it against the webhook SLA.

[10:29] Maren Banerjee: Okay, I want to be clear on customer exposure before we decide anything. Which accounts got late ETA pushes in the last 24 hours? Halvorsen's dispatch team has been asking about it on their side too.

[10:32] Noa Calloway: Two accounts with webhook subscriptions on Predict ETA. Halvorsen is one of them. Late pushes were mostly under 6 seconds, so their ETA board lagged but nothing dropped. No missed deliveries on our side. Arjun has the account list if we need to notify.

Key: PRED-1412
Type: Story
Priority: High
Status: In Progress
Assignee: Oskar Thorsby
Reporter: Leila Haddad
Component: Predict ETA / Models

Summary: PRED-1412: Ship ETA model v4.2 with multi-stop dwell features

Description

Predict ETA currently estimates dwell time at each stop using the carrier's historical average for that facility. For trucks that visit shared docks, where several carriers' appointments overlap, that average misses the queue effect and understates dwell during peak windows. Customers on multi-stop routes have reported ETAs that slip by 40 to 70 minutes at the second and third stops.

ETA model v4.2 adds a dwell-time feature for stops at shared docks. It uses the number of concurrent appointments in the dock window, the scheduled slot position, and the trailing 14-day median dwell at that dock. Features are computed from data already present in Dock Scheduler, so no new ingestion path is needed.

Rollout plan: general availability to all customers on July 14. Model shadow-scores for two weeks before that, with predictions logged but not shown.

Acceptance criteria
- Offline MAE on the standard ETA benchmark improves over v4.1 for multi-stop routes, with no regression on single-stop routes.
- Feature computation adds no more than 15 ms per stop at p95 in the scoring service.
- Shadow-scoring logs show no missing-feature rate above 0.5% for shared-dock stops.
- Rollback to v4.1 is possible by a config flag without a redeploy.

# Churn review: Q2 2026

**Date:** July 8, 2026, 11:06 UTC
**Author:** Esther Sorensen, Software Engineer
**Audience:** Customer Success, Support, Product, Sales leadership

## Summary

In Q2 we lost two logos. Both were regional fleet accounts on Northstar Track with Predict ETA enabled, and both had implementation stalled past 90 days before they cancelled. Neither account reached steady-state use of the dock module, and neither had a named internal owner on their side after the first month. This review covers what happened in each account, what the data shows about onboarding in general, and what we are changing.

## Account summaries

**Account A (regional carrier, 140 trucks at signing).** The telematics feed was connected in week two, but position data arrived with a gap of roughly forty minutes per truck every few hours. Support opened three tickets. Each was closed as "working as designed" after we confirmed the feed was within spec, but nobody on our side explained the gap to the customer's dispatch lead in plain terms. The customer's operations sponsor left the company in week six. Our follow-up cadence dropped to every two weeks, and the account went quiet.

**Account B (distribution fleet, 60 trucks at signing).** Track went live on time. Predict ETA was held back because the customer's stop data was missing addresses for about a third of delivery points. Our onboarding checklist did not flag this before go-live, so the ETA model ran on incomplete stops and produced estimates the customer's planners did not trust. Dock Scheduler was never configured. The customer concluded the product was not delivering the value promised in the sales cycle.

## What the pattern shows

Both accounts stalled in the same window: between weeks four and ten. In both, the first visible symptom was a data quality issue, not a product defect, and in both we discovered it late. Neither account was flagged as at risk on our health dashboard until the renewal conversation was already open.

Across the 2026 cohort so far, accounts that completed data validation within the first two weeks renewed at a notably higher rate than those that did not. The sample is small, so treat this as a direction, not a finding.

## Lessons for onboarding

1. **Validate stop and address data before go-live.** The checklist must block Predict ETA activation until address completeness passes a threshold we agree on with Product.
2. **Treat feed gaps as customer-facing events.** When Support closes a ticket as working as designed, the reply must explain the expected behavior in the customer's terms.
3. **Track named owners.** Each account needs a named operations contact and a backup. If the sponsor leaves, CSM is notified the same day.
4. **Alert on stalled implementation.** Any account with no completed milestone for 30 days should appear on the health dashboard automatically.
5. **Set dock module expectations early.** Several accounts buy Dock Scheduler for its value but never configure it. Make configuration a named milestone in the first 45 days.

## Actions

- Product (Leila Haddad) to define the address completeness threshold and gate ETA activation on it. Target: next sprint.
- Support (Noa Segal) to review the three Account A tickets and draft a plain-language explanation of the position gap for the feed documentation.
- Customer Success (Arjun Chaudry) to add the 30-day stall alert to the health dashboard and create the named-owner field in the CRM.
- Engineering to add a pre-go-live data validation report to the onboarding flow.

## Open questions

We have not yet confirmed whether Account A's position gap was caused by the carrier's ELD configuration or by our ingestion logic. Until that is resolved, we should not describe the gap as fully explained to anyone outside the team. I will update this review once the investigation closes.

# Customer Health Score Definition

**Author:** Tomas Baptiste, Solutions Engineer
**Date:** July 8, 2026
**Status:** Draft for review by Customer Success and Revenue Operations

## Purpose

This document defines the customer health score that Customer Success uses to rank the roughly 60 active accounts each week. The score is a single number from 0 to 100, with a color band for quick triage: green at 75 and above, amber from 50 to 74, and red below 50. It is meant to point CSMs to accounts that need attention. It is not a forecast of renewal and should not be quoted to customers.

## Inputs

The score combines four signals, each normalized to a 0 to 100 subscore and then weighted.

| Signal | Weight | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Product adoption | 40% | Platform usage logs |
| ETA usage | 25% | Predict ETA event logs |
| Support health | 20% | Support ticketing system |
| Executive engagement | 15% | CRM activity records |

### 1. Product adoption (40%)

Adoption is the share of licensed seats that are active in a given week. For Northstar Track and Dock Scheduler, the primary measure is **weekly active dispatchers**: unique users with a dispatcher role who log in and perform at least one action on a live shipment, a stop, or a dock appointment during the week.

The subscore equals weekly active dispatchers divided by licensed dispatcher seats, capped at 100. An account with 40 licensed seats and 30 weekly active dispatchers scores 75 on this component.

Accounts with Dock Scheduler but no Track license use dock-appointment actions only. Accounts with no dispatcher seats in the contract are scored on their weekly active users in the operations role, and this is flagged in the account record.

### 2. ETA usage (25%)

Predict ETA is only useful if dispatch acts on it. This subscore measures the share of stops in the week for which a predicted arrival was viewed or used to trigger a notification. A stop counts as used if a dispatcher opened its prediction, or if a customer-facing notification referencing the prediction was sent.

Accounts that are licensed for Predict ETA but show under 20 percent usage are flagged automatically for an enablement check.

### 3. Support health (20%)

This component starts at 100 and loses points for open issues. Each open Severity 1 ticket subtracts 30 points, each open Severity 2 ticket subtracts 10, and each Severity 3 ticket older than 14 days subtracts 3. The floor is 0.

Any account with an open Severity 1 ticket is shown with a red support flag in the CSM dashboard, regardless of the total score. The flag is a deliberate override because a single outage can matter more than any usage trend.

### 4. Executive engagement (15%)

This component measures whether the customer's leadership has been in contact with us recently. It scores 100 if a logged meeting or call with a customer executive occurred within the last 60 days, 60 if within the last 120 days, and 20 otherwise. Accounts with a named executive sponsor in the CRM receive a floor of 40.

## Calculation

The composite score is:

Health = 0.40 × Adoption + 0.25 × ETA usage + 0.20 × Support health + 0.15 × Executive engagement

The score is recalculated every Monday from the prior week's data and stored on the account record with a timestamp, so trends can be read week over week.

## Known limitations

- Telematics feed outages reduce ETA usage for affected accounts without any change in customer behavior. The data team should check feed status before a red ETA flag is acted on.
- Seasonal freight patterns can lower weekly active dispatchers for some accounts in slower months. CSMs should compare against the account's own trailing eight weeks.
- Executive engagement is only as good as CRM logging. Missing entries will look like disengagement.

## Next steps

- Revenue Operations to validate the weights against the last two quarters of renewal outcomes.
- Customer Success to review the amber threshold with the three largest accounts before rollout.
- Engineering to confirm that the weekly recalculation job reads from the production usage store, not the reporting replica.

# On-call handbook

**Owner:** Aaliyah Granholm, Sales Development Representative
**Last updated:** July 8, 2026
**Audience:** Engineering, Support, Operations, and anyone on a customer-facing escalation path

## Purpose

This handbook explains how on-call coverage works across our Oslo and Toronto teams, how to hand over an open incident, and when to wake the incident commander. It applies to production incidents affecting Northstar Track, Predict ETA, and Dock Scheduler. It does not cover routine support tickets, which follow the normal Support queue.

## How coverage works

We run a **follow-the-sun** model. Oslo owns on-call from 07:00 to 15:00 local time. Toronto picks up at 15:00 Oslo time and holds coverage until the Oslo shift starts the next morning. Each shift has one primary responder and one backup. The primary is the first person paged. The backup is paged if the primary does not acknowledge within ten minutes.

The overlap window, roughly 15:00 to 16:00 Oslo time, is where most handovers happen. Do not treat the overlap as optional. If an incident is open when a shift ends, the outgoing responder stays on the incident until the incoming responder confirms they have it.

The schedule lives in the **pager rotation**, which is maintained by Operations. Swaps are allowed, but both people must update the rotation at least 24 hours before the shift begins. Last-minute swaps are logged and reviewed by the Engineering manager on the affected team.

## Handing over an open incident

A handover is complete only when the incoming responder has acknowledged it in the incident channel. Use this checklist:

1. **Summarize the state.** One paragraph: what is broken, which customers are affected, and what has been ruled out.
2. **List the active actions.** Name any rollback, config change, or vendor ticket in progress and who owns it.
3. **Share the evidence.** Link the dashboards, log queries, and any affected truck or dock IDs.
4. **State the next decision point.** For example, "If the ETA error rate is still above threshold at 17:00 Oslo time, roll back the model version."
5. **Confirm the customer status.** Note whether a customer has been told, by whom, and what they were promised.

Post the handover summary in the incident channel, then ping the incoming responder directly. Do not rely on a status update alone.

## When to wake the incident commander

The incident commander (IC) is the person who coordinates response for any incident above a minimum severity. You should page the IC immediately if any of the following apply:

- Live tracking is unavailable for more than 15 percent of active trucks in any region.
- Predict ETA publishes arrival times that are visibly wrong for a large customer's whole fleet.
- Dock Scheduler double-books appointments at a customer site that is currently receiving freight.
- A customer reports a safety-relevant problem, such as a driver being sent to the wrong location during a hazmat load.
- The primary responder cannot resolve the issue within 60 minutes and has no clear path forward.

If you are unsure whether something qualifies, page the IC. A false alarm costs a few minutes of sleep. A missed escalation can cost a customer.

Do not wait for permission from a manager before paging the IC. The IC will decide whether to pull in additional people.

## During the incident

Keep updates in the incident channel, not in direct messages. Post every 30 minutes, even if the update is "no change." When a customer contacts Support about the incident, Support Lead, Tier 2 is the single point for customer messaging. Engineering should not reply to customers directly unless the Support Lead asks.

Record decisions as they happen. A short line such as "Rolled back model v4.2 at 16:40 Oslo time, owner: on-call primary" is more useful than a long reconstruction afterward.

## After the incident

Within two business days, the IC or the primary responder writes a short review covering timeline, impact, root cause if known, and follow-up items. Reviews are blameless. Follow-up items go into the normal Engineering backlog with an owner and a due date.

If the incident affected a customer contract, Customer Success should be looped in before the review is published.

## Questions

Ask in the #oncall-handover channel. Changes to this handbook go through Operations and are announced there.

# Renewal Playbook

**Owner:** Imani Zaragoza, Senior Software Engineer
**Last updated:** July 9, 2026, 16:46 UTC
**Applies to:** Account Executives, Customer Success Managers, Revenue Operations, Deal Desk

## Purpose

This playbook sets out how Northstar account teams run renewals. The goal is to start every renewal early enough that pricing, product usage and the customer's own budget cycle can all be addressed before the contract window closes. Renewals that start late tend to end in short extensions, discounts agreed under time pressure, or churn that could have been prevented.

## Timeline

Account teams start every renewal **120 days** before the contract end date. Revenue Operations flags the renewal in the CRM when the account enters that window, and the account owner confirms the start date within two business days.

The three stages below run in order, but they overlap. Most accounts are in the health review while the mutual action plan is being drafted.

## Stage 1: Mutual action plan

A **mutual action plan** is a shared document, agreed with the customer, that lists every step between now and signature. It names an owner on each side for every step, and each step has a date.

A good plan includes:

- The decision-maker and the approval path on the customer side, including procurement and finance
- Any changes to fleet size, product scope or locations expected during the term
- A review meeting with the customer's operations lead, not only the buyer
- The deal desk pricing review and the expected date of the pricing response
- The signature deadline, working backward from the contract end date

Share the plan with the customer within ten business days of entering the window. If the customer declines a formal plan, keep a written version internally and send a summary email after each call. Do not let the absence of a signed plan delay the health review.

## Stage 2: Health review

The health review answers one question: is this customer getting enough value to renew at the current scope? Customer Success Managers run it using the following inputs:

- **Usage:** Active trucks in Northstar Track, Predict ETA and Dock Scheduler compared with the contracted count. A drop of more than 10 percent over the last 90 days is a flag.
- **Prediction quality:** ETA accuracy at the stop level for the past quarter, as reported in the account dashboard. Attach a short explanation if the accuracy fell.
- **Support history:** Open and recently closed tickets, with priority and time to resolution. Summarize repeat issues instead of listing every ticket.
- **Stakeholders:** Whether the original champion is still in role. If not, identify the replacement within two weeks.
- **Sentiment:** The account owner's honest read, based on the last three calls or meetings.

Rate each account green, amber or red. Amber and red accounts get a recovery action with an owner and a date, added to the mutual action plan.

## Stage 3: Pricing check with deal desk

Before the renewal proposal goes to the customer, the account owner submits the proposed pricing to deal desk. Start from list prices: Northstar Track at $14, Predict ETA at $9 and Dock Scheduler at $6, each per truck per month. Document every discount with a reason code, and state the discount in both percentage and dollar terms in the proposal.

Deal desk reviews three things: whether the discount matches the health rating, whether the term length justifies any multi-year rate, and whether bundling changes the effective price per product. Red accounts may qualify for a restructured package rather than a straight discount, which deal desk can model before the proposal is written.

Allow five business days for the deal desk review. Build this into the timeline so that the pricing response arrives before the customer's own budget review.

## Roles

- **Account Executive:** Owns the renewal, the mutual action plan and the commercial terms.
- **Customer Success Manager:** Leads the health review and the recovery actions.
- **Revenue Operations:** Maintains renewal dates, flags and pipeline stages.
- **Deal Desk:** Approves discounts and restructured packages.
- **Product:** Consulted when a health review shows a feature gap that is blocking renewal.

## Reporting

Revenue Operations publishes a weekly renewal report listing every account in the window, its stage, its health rating and its next dated action. Accounts that miss a dated action for two consecutive weeks are escalated to the Chief Revenue Officer's staff meeting.

## Revision history

This playbook replaces the informal renewal guidance used in previous quarters. Suggestions for changes should go to Imani Zaragoza, with Revenue Operations copied, before the next quarterly review.

**ENG-8105: Retire legacy reporting service**

**Key:** ENG-8105
**Type:** Task
**Priority:** High
**Status:** In Progress
**Assignee:** Daniel Kimura
**Reporter:** Tamar Folau
**Component:** Platform / Reporting
**Created:** July 11, 2026, 17:02 UTC

---

**Description**

The legacy reporting service still runs alongside the reporting pipeline we built for Northstar Track and Predict ETA. It generates the weekly on-time arrival summaries and the per-lane dwell exports that a small number of customers still pull through their scheduled report links. Everything else in reporting has moved to the new pipeline, so this service now carries cost, on-call load, and a second copy of the truck-event schema that drifts from the primary one.

Over the last quarter we confirmed three things. First, the legacy service reads from a replica that is two schema versions behind, which is why the dwell exports occasionally omit stops with split appointments. Second, only four scheduled report links still resolve to legacy endpoints; the rest were migrated during Q2. Third, Support has not received a reporting-specific ticket that traces to the legacy path in the past 60 days.

This issue covers migrating the four remaining report links to the new pipeline, verifying output parity, and decommissioning the service and its replica.

**Context**

- Dock Scheduler appointment data is not read by the legacy service, so no changes are expected on that side.
- Output format for the weekly summary must stay byte-compatible with the current CSV layout, since two customer procurement teams parse it automatically.
- Noa Segal (Support Lead, Tier 2) has agreed to notify affected account contacts once the cutover date is set. Support will not need to open tickets on their behalf.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. All four remaining scheduled report links resolve to the new pipeline and return HTTP 200 for a test run against staging.
2. Parity check passes for the weekly on-time summary: row counts and field values match the legacy output for the last 4 full weeks of production data, with the known split-appointment stops explained in the diff notes.
3. Dwell export parity check passes for the same window, with the split-appointment fix verified.
4. Legacy service is set to read-only for 14 days with no requests from any customer-facing path before shutdown is scheduled.
5. The legacy replica is removed from the monitoring dashboard and its alerting rules are deleted.
6. Service, replica, and scheduled jobs are decommissioned, and the infrastructure definitions are removed from the repository.
7. The runbook page for the legacy service is archived, and a short note is added to the new pipeline runbook pointing to the migration history.

**Out of scope**

- Changes to the CSV layout or to any customer-facing report fields.
- Any work on Predict ETA model outputs; those are tracked separately.

---

**Tamar Folau** (July 11, 2026, 17:41 UTC)
Good. Note that the split-appointment bug is upstream of the replica lag, so the parity diff will look worse on the dwell export than on the summary. Please keep those two diffs separate in the write-up so Support can explain them cleanly.

# Release Notes: Predict ETA Model v4.2

**Date:** July 14, 2026, 15:30 UTC
**Author:** Theo Wexley, Technical Writer
**Reviewed by:** Leila Haddad, Product Manager, Predict ETA

## Overview

On July 14, we rolled out ETA model v4.2 to all Predict ETA customers. This release improves arrival-time predictions for every stop on your routes and introduces a new dwell-time feature. No action is required on your part. Predictions update automatically in Track and Dock Scheduler.

## What's new

### Dwell-time feature

The model now estimates how long a truck will remain at each stop, including loading, unloading, and waiting time. Dwell estimates feed directly into the predicted arrival time for downstream stops, so a delay at one location is reflected in the ETAs for the stops that follow. Dispatch teams can see the dwell estimate alongside each predicted arrival.

## Accuracy improvements

On our internal benchmark, ETA model v4.2 shows a 12% lower mean absolute error compared with v4.1. The largest gains appear on multi-stop routes, where earlier errors compounded across legs.

## What you need to do

Nothing. The update applies to all active accounts. Existing integrations, webhooks, and dock appointment settings are unchanged.

## Questions

If you notice predictions that look unusual after July 14, contact Northstar Support and include the shipment ID and the stop in question. Our Support team will review the case with the ML group.

**Description**

**Context**

Large shipment-history CSV exports from Northstar Track are timing out in the web session. Customers with fleets above roughly 400 trucks and a 90-day window hit the gateway timeout before the file is generated. Support has logged eleven such cases since the start of the quarter, and two of them were from accounts on the renewal list this month.

The first fix shipped last week and raised the synchronous limit, but it only moved the failure point. Exports above the new limit still fail, and the retry behavior makes the gateway load worse. This follow-up moves CSV generation to a background job. The user requests the export, sees a status row in the Exports panel, and receives an email with a signed download link when the file is ready.

**Scope**

- Queue export requests to the existing job runner, with one queue per tenant to avoid starving smaller accounts.
- Store the generated file in the object store with a 7-day expiry on the signed link.
- Add an Exports panel row showing queued, running, complete, or failed.
- Email the requester on completion. Failed jobs email the requester and the Support queue.

Out of scope: changes to the Predict ETA export format and the Dock Scheduler appointment export, which Leila Haddad's team is handling separately.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. A 90-day export for a 600-truck fleet completes without a gateway timeout.
2. The web request returns within 2 seconds with a job ID.
3. The Exports panel shows accurate status for each job transition, including retries.
4. The download link works for the requester only and expires after 7 days.
5. A failed job produces a visible error message and a Support notification; no partial file is delivered.
6. Existing synchronous exports under 10,000 rows keep working unchanged, so no one on the current workflow has to change anything.
7. Unit and integration tests cover queueing, completion, failure, and expiry.

Wren Kinsella owns the job implementation and the Exports panel changes. Alma Devereux owns the queue capacity and alerting configuration. Noa Segal's Tier 2 team will need updated macros before release.

# How Predict ETA Works

**Audience:** Account teams (Sales, Customer Success, Support)
**Author:** Rosa Inoue, Sales Development Representative
**Date:** July 16, 2026

This explainer covers what Predict ETA does, what goes into its estimates, and how to describe it to customers accurately. Use it as a reference before calls with logistics or dispatch teams. For technical depth, send questions to Product (Leila Haddad) or the ETA models team (Oskar Thorsby).

## What Predict ETA does

Predict ETA produces an arrival-time estimate for every stop on a shipment. It runs alongside Northstar Track, which shows where a truck is, and Dock Scheduler, which manages appointments at the warehouse. Track tells a customer where the truck is now. Predict ETA tells them when it will reach the next stop and the stop after that. Each estimate is updated as new data arrives, so the number on screen can move during a trip.

Predict ETA is priced at $9 per truck per month at list price.

## How the model works

The core model is a **gradient-boosted** decision tree ensemble. In plain terms, it builds many small prediction trees one after another, where each new tree corrects the errors left by the ones before it. We chose this approach because it handles mixed inputs well (numbers like distance, categories like lane and carrier, and time-of-day effects) and because its behavior is easier to inspect than many alternatives. Customers do not need to understand the mechanics, but account teams should know it is a trained statistical model, not a fixed formula, and it improves as more shipment history accumulates.

The model combines four families of input:

1. **Live position.** GPS and ELD positions from the telematics feed, sampled as frequently as the device provides them. Position alone gives remaining distance to a stop.
2. **Traffic.** Current and expected road speeds along the remaining route, including recurring congestion patterns for the time of day and day of week.
3. **Historical dwell time.** How long trucks have typically spent at a given site before departing, measured from arrival to departure. This is one of the most important inputs for stop-level accuracy. A dock that averages long unloading times will produce later departure estimates even when the drive is clear. Dwell time is calculated per site and per carrier type where the data supports it, and it is refreshed as new visits are recorded.
4. **Driver hours.** Remaining legal driving and on-duty time reported through the ELD. If a driver must take a mandated break before the next stop, the estimate reflects it. Without this input, estimates for long hauls would be consistently optimistic.

The model outputs an estimated arrival window, not a single guaranteed time. The window widens for stops that are far away or where dwell data is thin.

## What the model does not do

- It does not know about events it has not been told about, such as a breakdown that is not reported through the telematics feed, a weather closure, or a dock that has been shut without a schedule change.
- It does not override a dispatcher's manual change. If a customer's dispatch team edits a route in their own system and that edit does not come through to Northstar, the estimate will be based on the old plan.
- It is not a service-level commitment. Do not describe estimates as guaranteed arrival times in proposals or contract language. Use "predicted" and "estimated" consistently.

## Talking to customers

Lead with the business outcome: fewer missed appointments, less time waiting at docks, and earlier notice to receiving teams. When a customer asks how accurate it is, direct them to the accuracy reports in the Predict ETA dashboard, which show performance by lane and by site. Avoid quoting a single accuracy percentage unless Product has approved it for that account.

If a customer's data is sparse (new lanes, few historical visits), say so plainly. Estimates improve over the first few weeks as dwell and traffic history builds up. Setting that expectation in advance prevents early disappointment.

## Questions and escalation

For pricing or packaging questions, contact Priya Kaplan. For technical questions about model inputs or accuracy, contact Leila Haddad. For a customer reporting consistently wrong estimates on a specific lane, open a Support ticket with the shipment IDs and time window so the ETA models team can review the inputs.

**TRK-2220: Shipment timeline virtualization**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Key | TRK-2220 |
| Type | Story |
| Priority | High |
| Status | In Progress |
| Assignee | Olu Trujillo |
| Reporter | Dara Palmer |
| Component | Northstar Track, Web Client |
| Created | July 19, 2026, 08:01 UTC |

**Description**

**Context**

The shipment detail view in Northstar Track renders every event on a shipment's timeline as a DOM node. For long-haul shipments with dense telematics feeds, a single timeline can hold several thousand events: position pings, geofence crossings, door open and close signals, and Predict ETA revisions. Customers with large fleets have reported that the page takes more than eight seconds to become interactive, and scrolling drops to single-digit frame rates on mid-range laptops in dispatch offices.

Last week's profiling confirmed that layout and paint dominate the cost, not data fetching. Median payload size for the timeline endpoint is acceptable. The problem is what we do with it on the client.

**Proposal**

Virtualize the timeline list so that only the rows inside the viewport plus a small overscan buffer are mounted. Keep the full event array in the store so filtering, search, and export continue to operate on complete data. Row heights for event types are fixed today, so we can use fixed-height windowing for the first pass and defer variable-height support.

Out of scope for this ticket:
- Changes to the timeline API or pagination
- Server-side aggregation of position pings (tracked separately)
- Redesign of the map panel

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A shipment with 10,000 timeline events renders its first visible rows in under 1.5 seconds on the reference laptop profile used in the performance suite.
- [ ] Scrolling holds at 55 fps or better across the full timeline on that profile.
- [ ] No more than 80 timeline row components are mounted at any time, verified by a unit test that counts mounted nodes.
- [ ] Keyboard navigation (up, down, page up, page down, home, end) moves focus through all events, including those not currently mounted.
- [ ] Browser find (Ctrl+F) is replaced by an in-app search that returns matches across the full timeline and scrolls the matched row into view.
- [ ] Export to CSV includes every event, not only rendered rows. Verified against a shipment with 10,000 events.
- [ ] Screen reader announces the total event count and current position in the list.
- [ ] Existing timeline snapshot tests are updated or replaced; no regressions in the events-by-type filter.

**Notes**

Predict ETA revision events arrive out of order when a carrier resends a batch. The virtualized list must sort by event timestamp in the store, not by insertion order, so that the window stays stable when late events arrive. Leila Haddad has confirmed the revision event schema will not change in this quarter.

---

**DOCK-651: Waitlist for cancelled slots**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Key | DOCK-651 |
| Type | Story |
| Priority | Medium |
| Status | In Progress |
| Assignee | Anika Delacroix |
| Reporter | Noa Yeboah |
| Component | Dock Scheduler, Appointments |
| Created | July 20, 2026, 18:06 UTC |

**Description**

*Context*

Dock Scheduler customers book dock appointments for inbound and outbound trucks. When a carrier cancels an appointment, the freed slot currently sits empty until the warehouse team notices it and manually offers it to another carrier. In Q3 we had repeated feedback from larger warehouse accounts that cancelled slots often go unused for hours, even when other carriers on the same day are asking for earlier windows.

This ticket adds a waitlist. When a slot is cancelled, Dock Scheduler should offer it to waitlisted carriers in order, and the warehouse should be able to see and manage the queue from the dock calendar.

*Scope*

- Carriers can join a waitlist for a fully booked window on a given dock door.
- On cancellation, the slot is offered to the first waitlisted carrier whose vehicle type and trailer requirements match the slot.
- The offer expires after a configurable hold period. If it expires or is declined, the next carrier is offered the slot.
- Warehouse dispatchers can view, reorder, and remove waitlist entries.

*Out of scope*

- Predict ETA changes. Arrival predictions are not affected by waitlist assignments in this ticket.
- Pricing or billing changes. Waitlist use is included in the existing Dock Scheduler per-truck plan.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. A carrier can join and leave a waitlist for a booked window through the API and the carrier portal.
2. When a confirmed appointment is cancelled, the freed slot is offered to the first matching waitlisted carrier within one minute.
3. An offer holds the slot for the configured period. Expiry or decline moves the offer to the next carrier with no manual step.
4. Dispatchers can reorder or remove waitlist entries from the dock calendar.
5. Every offer, acceptance, decline, and expiry is written to the appointment audit log with a timestamp.
6. If no matching carrier is waitlisted, the slot returns to open inventory and is visible to standard booking within the same minute.
7. Existing bookings and cancellations behave exactly as before for accounts that do not enable the waitlist.

**Owner and status**

Anika Delacroix owns the data model and the matching logic. Noa Yeboah owns the API and the notification flow. Status is In Progress; the data model migration is done in staging, and the matching logic is in review.

**PRED-1307: Driver hours of service in predictions**

**Key:** PRED-1307
**Type:** Bug
**Priority:** High
**Status:** In Progress
**Assignee:** Oskar Thorsby
**Reporter:** Noa Grimaldi
**Component:** Predict ETA / ETA models
**Labels:** hos, customer-escalation

---

**Description**

**Context**

Predict ETA currently assumes a truck keeps moving at the planned speed until it reaches the next stop. For fleets with regulated drivers, that assumption breaks when a driver reaches the end of a legal driving window. The driver must take a required rest break, or the shift must end, and the truck sits idle until a relief driver or a restart is available. Our predictions do not model that gap, so ETAs for affected stops are too early, sometimes by several hours.

Halvorsen Freight Group raised this last week. Their dispatch team (Ingrid Solberg) reported that three routes showed arrival times that the drivers could not legally meet, and two customer receiving docks were booked against those times. The dock conflicts were resolved manually, but the pattern is repeatable on any long-haul route with a single driver.

The ELD feed we already ingest includes duty status changes and remaining driving time, but the ETA model does not read those fields. Hours-of-service state is currently dropped at the normalization step.

**Proposed approach**

1. Pass remaining driving time and current duty status from the ELD feed into the feature pipeline.
2. Add a rest-stop insertion step to the route simulation: when projected driving time would exceed the remaining window, insert a rest break at the nearest eligible location and shift downstream stops.
3. Flag predictions that depend on a driver change so dispatch can see the assumption.

**Acceptance criteria**

- For a single-driver route that exceeds the remaining driving window, the predicted arrival for every stop after the window is at least the rest-break duration later than the no-HOS baseline.
- Predictions for trucks with no ELD hours data fall back to the current model and carry a visible "HOS unknown" flag.
- Replay of the Halvorsen Freight Group routes from last week's report produces ETAs within the actual observed range.
- No regression in median absolute error for the standard test set (non-regulated and team-driver routes).
- Dock Scheduler appointment suggestions consume the new ETAs without code changes on its side.

**Out of scope:** Recalculating rest-stop locations from live traffic. That is tracked separately.

**Summary:** Load test for morning wave

**Description**

**Context**

Customers in the Northstar Track and Predict ETA rollout have started sending telematics batches in a tighter window before the early shift. Over the last several weeks, the morning window (roughly 05:00 to 08:00 in each customer's local time) has produced the highest ingest volume of the day, and two accounts have reported delayed ETA refreshes during that period. Dock Scheduler appointment syncs for the same accounts slowed at the same time, which suggests a shared bottleneck upstream of the ETA model, not in the model itself.

We do not yet have a reproducible picture of where the queue backs up. This ticket covers a controlled load test that replays a representative morning wave against staging at 1.5x observed peak, so we can see which stage saturates first.

**Scope**

- Replay anonymized telematics feeds from the top twelve accounts by truck count, preserving their per-minute shape from the morning window.
- Measure end-to-end latency from ELD ingest to refreshed predicted arrival for each stop.
- Measure Dock Scheduler appointment sync lag during the same run.
- Capture queue depth, consumer lag and worker CPU at each stage.

Out of scope: changes to the ETA model weights and any production configuration change.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. The load test runs to completion at 1.5x observed peak for a full simulated morning window without manual restarts.
2. p95 ingest-to-ETA latency is reported per account and per stage, with the first saturated stage identified.
3. Dock Scheduler sync lag is reported at the same load, with the p95 and maximum values recorded.
4. No data loss: record counts at ingest match record counts at the ETA store within 0.01%.
5. A written summary lists the top three recommended changes, each with an estimated effort in engineering days.
6. Results are posted to the Predict ETA channel and linked from this ticket.

**Owner and status**

Alma Devereux owns the test harness and the run. Wren Kinsella owns the replay dataset and the analysis. The ticket is In Progress: the harness is built, the dataset has been anonymized and reviewed, and the first dry run completed without errors on the ingest side.

# Onboarding Playbook for Fleets Over 1,000 Trucks

*Author: Lars Amsel, Support Specialist | Last updated July 27, 2026*

## Purpose

This playbook describes how Support and Customer Success run onboarding for fleets of more than 1,000 trucks. Large fleets carry more integration risk than smaller accounts, and a mistake in one depot can spread across the whole network. The phased approach below keeps the rollout contained and gives each phase a clear exit criterion. The standard path is a six-week rollout, with each phase gated on the one before it.

Use this playbook for accounts that will run Northstar Track across the full fleet. Predict ETA and Dock Scheduler can be added at any phase, but they should not delay the core tracking go-live.

## Phase 1: ELD Connection (Weeks 1 to 2)

The customer's ELD provider must authorize our data feed before anything else can happen. Start this in the kickoff call, because the customer's IT team often needs two to three weeks to approve third-party access.

Exit criteria:
- Feed authorization is signed by the customer's security owner.
- Positions for at least 95% of active trucks appear in Northstar Track within 60 seconds.
- Unmatched vehicle IDs are listed in a shared sheet, and the customer has assigned an owner for each.

Do not move to Phase 2 with unmatched IDs unresolved. They become blind spots on the dispatch board.

## Phase 2: Pilot Depot (Weeks 3 to 4)

Select one depot with 80 to 150 trucks, ideally one with an engaged operations lead and a mix of local and long-haul routes. Enable Predict ETA for that depot's stops only. Compare predicted arrival times with actual arrivals daily and share the accuracy report with the depot manager.

Exit criteria:
- Predicted arrival accuracy within the agreed window for at least 85% of stops over five consecutive working days.
- No open severity-one tickets.
- The depot manager signs off in writing.

If accuracy falls short, check first for stop geocoding errors and for drivers who log arrivals late. Escalate model questions to Product (Predict ETA) only after those checks.

## Phase 3: Dispatcher Training (Week 5)

Train dispatchers in groups of no more than 12. Sessions run 90 minutes and cover live tracking, exception alerts, and the appointment workflow in Dock Scheduler if the account uses it. Each dispatcher completes a short practical task in the sandbox before go-live.

Exit criteria:
- Every dispatcher on the schedule has completed training.
- The customer has named a super-user for each shift.
- Support has a shared escalation path for the first two weeks of full use.

## Phase 4: Full Fleet (Week 6)

Enable the remaining depots in two waves, with no more than half the fleet changing on any single day. Keep the pilot depot as the reference for expected behavior. Hold a daily 15-minute check-in with the customer's operations lead through the end of the week.

Exit criteria:
- All active trucks report positions.
- Open tickets are below the threshold agreed at kickoff.
- The customer's operations lead confirms go-live in writing.

## Roles

- **Customer Success Manager:** owns the plan, the schedule, and the exit reviews.
- **Support Engineer:** owns feed health, ID matching, and integration tickets.
- **Support Lead, Tier 2:** approves any change to the phase gates.
- **Product:** consulted on Predict ETA accuracy questions.

## Common Risks

Large fleets tend to fail in predictable ways: duplicate vehicle IDs after a merger, drivers who share tablets, and depots that run on paper appointment sheets. Flag these in the kickoff call and assign owners. If a phase slips by more than one week, notify the account's executive sponsor the same day.

**Description**

Orchard Lane Fleet Services reports that temperature alerts for their refrigerated trailers are arriving late or not at all. Their dispatch team relies on these alerts to divert loads before product spoils, and they have had two loads flagged after the fact by their receiving sites. The issue was raised in NS-4314 and escalated to engineering on July 28.

Their fleet sends temperature readings through the telematics feed into Northstar Track. Alerts should fire when a reading stays outside the configured band for longer than the configured dwell time. For this account the dwell time is set to 10 minutes.

**Context from support**

- Alerts appear in the portal timeline but the push notifications to the dispatch console are delayed, sometimes by more than 40 minutes.
- The affected trucks all report through the same telematics gateway. Trucks on the second gateway appear unaffected.
- Last week the customer changed their reporting interval from 60 seconds to 30 seconds to get finer detail. The delays started within a day of that change.

**Reproduction steps**

1. Create a test fleet with a reefer truck reporting at a 30-second interval.
2. Set a temperature band of 2 to 8 degrees Celsius with a 10-minute dwell time.
3. Replay a feed in which the temperature rises to 11 degrees and holds for 15 minutes.
4. Observe the alert timestamp in the portal and the push delivery time to the dispatch console.
5. Compare against the same replay at a 60-second interval.

**Acceptance criteria**

**Description**

Predict ETA currently treats every stop as a single-leg drive-time estimate. Leila Haddad's team has confirmed that the model needs explicit border crossing features before we can tighten the ETA confidence band for these lanes.

- Add a border crossing feature set: crossing point ID, historical dwell percentiles by crossing and hour of day, and crossing-day type (weekday, weekend, holiday).

3. Shadow evaluation on last quarter's cross-border shipments shows a reduction in mean absolute ETA error on lanes with crossings. The threshold is set with the ETA model team.
4. Flag off reproduces current production predictions exactly.

**TRK-2247: Webhook backoff with jitter**

**Key:** TRK-2247
**Type:** Story
**Priority:** High
**Status:** In Progress
**Assignee:** Yara Santana
**Reporter:** Elif Atwater
**Component:** Track / Webhooks

**Description**

When a customer's webhook endpoint returns a 5xx or times out, Track currently retries every 30 seconds with no variation. When several subscriber endpoints fail at once, our retries arrive in synchronized bursts. Last week, one fleet customer's receiving service went down again under our retry load after recovering from an unrelated incident. We need retries that spread out over time and back off as failures continue.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Retry delay grows exponentially from a 30-second base, capped at 15 minutes.
- Full jitter is applied to every computed delay, so two events that failed together do not retry together.
- If the response includes a `Retry-After` header, the delay is at least that value.
- After 10 failed attempts, the event moves to the dead-letter queue and the subscriber is notified in the delivery dashboard.
- Delivery logs record attempt number, computed delay, and jitter seed for each retry.
- Existing 2xx and 4xx handling is unchanged.

# Data retention policy

**Owner:** Emeka Ibekwe, Support Engineer
**Last updated:** August 9, 2026, 16:14 UTC
**Applies to:** Northstar Track, Predict ETA, Dock Scheduler

## Purpose

This document describes how Northstar Systems keeps vehicle position history and related shipment data, how long we keep it, and how customers can ask us to remove it. Support, Customer Success, and Engineering should use it when answering customer questions or handling a request. If this document conflicts with a signed customer agreement, the agreement governs.

## What counts as position history

Position history is the time-stamped location data we receive from ELD and telematics feeds for each truck. It includes:

- GPS coordinates and heading as reported by the feed
- Speed and ignition events, where the customer's feed provides them
- Stop arrival and departure times recorded against a shipment
- Dock appointment records created in Dock Scheduler that reference a truck or trailer

Predict ETA training data is derived from position history. Derived features are retained under the same schedule as the source data they came from.

## Retention schedule

Position history is kept for **13 months** from the time each point was recorded. After that window, the records are purged in the nightly job and cannot be restored from backup. Backups follow the same 13-month window, so a purged record will not reappear in a later restore.

Shipment and appointment metadata, such as shipment IDs, customer-entered reference numbers, and dock names, is kept for as long as the account is active. When an account closes, that metadata is purged 90 days after the end of the contract term unless the customer has asked for an earlier date in writing.

Aggregated, de-identified metrics, such as on-time arrival rates for a region, may be kept longer. They must not contain vehicle identifiers, driver identifiers, or precise coordinates.

## Customer deletion requests

Customers can file a deletion request at any time. A deletion request can cover all position history for one account, all records for a specific vehicle or driver identifier, or a date range inside the retention window. Customers do not need to explain the reason.

To file a request, the customer's administrator submits it through the support portal or emails support. Support confirms the scope in writing with the requester before processing. Confirmation should name the account, the scope, and the earliest and latest dates affected.

Once confirmed, Engineering runs the deletion against primary storage within 30 days. Deleted data is also removed from backups as they age out, and no later than the end of the 13-month window. The ticket stays open until Engineering confirms completion, and Support sends the customer a closing note that describes what was removed and what, if anything, was retained for legal reasons.

Some records cannot be deleted immediately. Invoices and tax records are kept by Finance under separate rules. Records held under a legal hold are not deleted until the hold is released, and Legal notifies Support when that happens.

## Handling notes for staff

- Do not promise deletion on a specific day. Use the 30-day processing window.
- Do not restore purged position history for a customer, even from backup, unless Legal has approved it in writing.
- If a customer asks for data older than 13 months, explain that it is no longer retained and point them to any exports they took earlier.
- Log every deletion request in the compliance tracker, including requests that are withdrawn.
- If you are unsure whether a record falls inside the policy, escalate to Support Lead, Tier 2 before responding.

## Open items

- Confirm with Engineering that Predict ETA model artifacts trained on expired data are rebuilt on the normal training cycle, not on a separate schedule.
- Add a self-service option for deletion requests to the admin console next quarter.
- Review whether Dock Scheduler appointment history needs the same 13-month window or a shorter one.
