# Support Escalation Runbook

**Owner:** Viktor Lehtonen, Data Engineer
**Last updated:** August 10, 2026, 08:12 UTC
**Audience:** Support, Customer Success, Engineering on-call, Product

## Purpose

This runbook explains how the Support team grades the severity of an incoming issue, who is paged at each level, and what response times apply. It covers Northstar Track, Predict ETA, and Dock Scheduler. Use it whenever a ticket may need engineering attention outside normal support hours.

Severity is set by customer impact, not by how loudly the customer describes the problem. A quiet report that stops dispatch is more serious than a loud complaint about a cosmetic issue.

## Severity Levels

**Severity 1 (critical).** Production is down or materially broken for a customer, with no workaround. Examples:
- Live tracking is missing for all or most trucks in an account.
- Predict ETA returns no arrival times for active routes.
- Dock Scheduler blocks all appointment bookings at one or more sites.
- Data is being written incorrectly to a customer's systems.

**Severity 2 (major).** A core function is degraded, or a large subset of users is affected, but a workaround exists. Examples: delayed position updates for one ELD provider, ETA accuracy complaints tied to a specific lane.

**Severity 3 (minor).** A single user or a non-core feature is affected. Examples: a report export fails, a dock label prints in the wrong order.

**Severity 4 (request).** Questions, feature requests, and documentation gaps.

When in doubt between two levels, pick the higher one and downgrade after triage. Never downgrade a ticket because the customer has been waiting a long time.

## Response Targets

| Severity | First response | Engineering owner | Customer update cadence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Severity 1 | Within 30 minutes, 24/7 | Named the same day | Every 60 minutes |
| Severity 2 | Within 4 business hours | Named within 1 business day | Daily |
| Severity 3 | Within 1 business day | Assigned in the normal queue | Weekly or on change |
| Severity 4 | Within 2 business days | Not required | On change |

A first response means a human has acknowledged the ticket and posted a next step. An automated reply does not count.

## Paging

Severity 1 tickets page the Engineering on-call rotation through the on-call paging tool. The Support Engineer on shift opens the page, attaches the ticket link, and confirms the account name and the affected products in the first message.

If on-call does not acknowledge within 15 minutes, page the secondary engineer, then the Engineering manager on duty. Support Lead, Tier 2 has authority to escalate directly to the Staff ML Engineer for Predict ETA problems.

Severity 2 tickets go to the Support Engineer queue and are reviewed at the next triage stand-up. Severity 3 and 4 tickets are handled in the normal queue.

## Ownership

Every Severity 1 ticket gets a named engineering owner the same day it is opened. The owner is responsible for diagnosis, the fix or mitigation, and the written summary. If the owner changes shift, they must hand off in the ticket with the current status, what has been tried, and the customer's last acknowledged expectation.

Customer Success is informed on every Severity 1 ticket for accounts with more than 20 trucks. The account's Customer Success Manager posts the customer-facing update.

## Closing and Review

A Severity 1 ticket is closed only after the customer confirms service is restored, or after 24 hours of stable operation with no new reports. Within three business days, the owner posts a short review in the ticket: timeline, root cause, customer impact, and follow-up items. Follow-ups are filed as Jira issues and linked back.

## Changes to This Runbook

Propose changes to Viktor Lehtonen. Changes to response targets require sign-off from the Support Lead, Tier 2 and the Engineering manager on duty.

**Description**

When a dispatcher switches the map from one region to another in Northstar Track, the client sometimes renders tiles from the previous region for several seconds. Trucks appear plotted on the wrong roads, and stop markers can sit outside their real service area. Two fleet customers reported this last week, and one dispatcher described it as "ghost roads."

Root cause is likely that the tile cache keys on zoom and bounding box only. It does not include the region ID, so a region switch within the same viewport reuses stale entries. The cache also skips eviction when the region change event arrives after the first tile request.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. Region ID is part of every tile cache key.
2. Switching regions clears or bypasses cached tiles for the previous region within 200 ms.
3. No tiles from the previous region render after a switch, including during slow network conditions.
4. Repeat switches between two regions show no cache growth beyond the configured limit.
5. Regression tests cover switching, rapid toggling, and offline-to-online recovery.

# Partner Program Overview

**Author:** Daniel Okafor, Chief Revenue Officer
**Date:** August 13, 2026, 16:30 UTC
**Audience:** Sales, Customer Success, Finance, Revenue Operations

## Purpose

This document describes how Northstar Systems works with outside firms that bring us business or help customers go live. The program has two tracks. Referral partners introduce new fleet and distribution prospects to us. Implementation partners deploy and configure Northstar Track, Predict ETA and Dock Scheduler for customers who need hands-on help at onboarding. The two tracks have different qualification bars and different payment terms, and this document covers both.

## Program tracks

**Referral partners** are firms that refer a qualified opportunity to our sales team. They do not touch the product or the customer's data. Their job ends when the opportunity is accepted into our pipeline and a contract is signed.

**Implementation partners** are firms that perform onboarding work: feed setup from ELD and telematics sources, stop and geofence configuration, dock calendar mapping, and user training. They sign a partner agreement and must complete our certification before they can be listed as an implementation partner on a customer order.

Some firms do both. A partner that refers a deal and then implements it is paid under each track separately, and the referral fee does not depend on whether the partner later implements.

## Qualification

### Referral partners

A referral partner is approved when it meets all of the following:

- A signed referral agreement with Northstar Systems, reviewed by Legal.
- A named partner lead who has completed our product overview session.
- At least one referred opportunity that Sales has accepted as a qualified lead. Acceptance means the account has a real fleet size, a named decision maker, and a stated need that our products address.
- No open conflict with an existing account. Revenue Operations checks the account list before any referral is accepted.

Referrals are logged in the CRM with the partner's ID on the opportunity. If a prospect is already in our pipeline before the referral arrives, the earlier record stands and the referral is not paid.

### Implementation partners

An implementation partner must:

- Sign the partner agreement and the data handling addendum.
- Complete certification, which covers Northstar Track feed configuration, Predict ETA setup, and Dock Scheduler appointment rules. Certification is run by Customer Success and takes about two days of hands-on work.
- Maintain at least one certified engineer on staff. If that engineer leaves, the partner has thirty days to certify a replacement before its status is reviewed.

Implementation partners do not get access to customer production accounts beyond what the implementation requires. Access is granted per project and removed at handover.

## Payment terms

### Referral fees

Referral fees are paid once, on the first full month of invoiced subscription revenue from a referred account. The fee is 10 percent of the first contract year's net subscription value, paid after the customer's first invoice has been collected. Fees are not paid on implementation services, on pass-through hardware, or on overage charges.

### Implementation fees

Implementation partners set their own project rates with the customer. Northstar does not pay implementation partners directly. Instead, a partner that completes certification and a signed project is listed on the customer order, and receives a 5 percent partner credit on Northstar Track and Predict ETA list price for the first contract year. Dock Scheduler is excluded from the credit because its onboarding is short and mostly handled by our own team.

### Clawback

If a referred customer cancels within twelve months of signing, the referral fee is reclaimed in full. If an implementation partner's project is reopened for defects traced to partner work, the partner credit is held until the defects are resolved.

## Governance

Priya Kaplan maintains the partner rate card and reviews any exception to these terms. Selin Yilmaz owns the partner registry in the CRM and runs the quarterly reconciliation with Finance. Exceptions above the standard terms need written approval from Daniel Okafor and Ruth Lindqvist.

Partner performance is reviewed each quarter. Partners that refer no qualified opportunities for two consecutive quarters are moved to inactive status. Implementation partners with two or more defect-related reopenings in a year are reviewed for certification renewal.

## Open items

Legal is finalizing the updated data handling addendum. Until it is signed off, implementation partners work under the existing addendum with the additional restriction that no production telematics exports leave the customer's environment. Questions go to Selin Yilmaz in Revenue Operations.

# Incident review: carrier API outage on July 22

**Author:** Mateo Koenig (Solutions Engineer, Northstar Systems)
**Date:** August 14, 2026, 11:12 UTC
**Status:** Final
**Scope:** Carrier integration ingestion service, Northstar Track

## Summary

On July 22, the inbound feed from one of our carrier partners' APIs stopped accepting connections for 47 minutes. During that window, Northstar Track did not receive position updates for trucks reporting through that carrier, and Predict ETA could not refresh arrival estimates for affected stops. The cause was an expired TLS client certificate that our integration service used to authenticate to the carrier. No data was lost. Updates queued on the carrier side and were backfilled once the connection recovered.

This review is blameless. It focuses on how the system and our processes allowed a foreseeable expiry to reach production, and on what we will change.

## Impact

- Roughly 1,900 truck positions were delayed. All were backfilled within 15 minutes of recovery.
- Eleven customer accounts saw stale tracking data for their carrier-sourced fleets. Two customers opened tickets; both were answered during the incident.
- Predict ETA recalculated arrival times for affected stops after backfill. Estimates generated during the outage were marked low-confidence in the dashboard.
- No dock appointments were missed. Dock Scheduler does not depend on the carrier feed.

## Timeline (UTC)

- **13:20** Ingestion service begins logging handshake failures to the carrier endpoint.
- **13:24** Automated alert fires on a rising error rate. It routes to the on-call queue, which was not yet acknowledged.
- **13:31** On-call engineer acknowledges and begins triage. Initial hypothesis is a carrier-side outage.
- **13:38** Carrier status page shows no incident. Engineer checks our client certificate and finds it expired at 13:00.
- **13:44** Renewed certificate is generated and staged. Rollout to ingestion pods begins.
- **14:07** Connections restored. Backfill starts.
- **14:12** Backfill completes. Customer-facing status updated.

## Root cause

The certificate was issued with a one-year validity and was renewed manually. The renewal was tracked in a personal calendar reminder rather than in our certificate inventory. There was no automated check that alerted on upcoming expiry, and the ingestion alert measured error rate only, so the first signal was production traffic failing.

## What went well

- The alert fired within four minutes of the first failure.
- The on-call engineer checked our own credentials before escalating to the carrier, which shortened diagnosis.
- Backfill was complete before most customers noticed the gap.
- Support posted a status update within 20 minutes of the first customer ticket.

## What went poorly

- The alert was not acknowledged for seven minutes, and the first hypothesis pointed outward.
- The runbook for carrier connectivity did not list certificate expiry as a check.
- Customers learned about the outage from their own dashboards before we posted a notice.

## Action items

1. **Certificate inventory and expiry alerts.** Move all client and service certificates into the central inventory with automated alerts at 30, 14, and 7 days before expiry. Owner: Platform team. Due next quarter.
2. **Automated renewal for carrier credentials.** Where the carrier supports it, renew automatically with a staged rollout. Owner: Integrations team.
3. **Expiry as a first-class check.** Add certificate validity to the ingestion health check and the connectivity runbook. Owner: Mateo Koenig.
4. **Alert on data freshness.** Add an alert when no positions arrive from a carrier for 10 minutes, independent of error rate. Owner: Platform team.
5. **Customer notice template.** Prepare a pre-approved status message for feed delays. Owner: Support Lead, Tier 2.

We will report progress on items 1 through 4 in the Q3 operations review.

5. Every provisioning event appears in the customer's audit log with actor, action, group, and timestamp.

**PRED-1467: ETA drift on multi-stop routes after model v4.2**

**Key:** PRED-1467
**Type:** Bug
**Priority:** High
**Status:** In Progress
**Assignee:** Oskar Thorsby
**Reporter:** Oskar Thorsby
**Component:** Predict ETA / ETA models
**Linked issues:** NS-4871, NS-4955, NS-4979
**Created:** August 19, 2026, 10:10 UTC

---

**Description**

Since model v4.2 shipped, predicted arrival times drift later as the number of stops on a route increases. On single-stop routes the error is within the agreed band. On routes with four or more stops it grows roughly linearly, and customers on dock-heavy lanes have reported arrivals that are consistently 20 to 40 minutes off by the final stop.

Root cause (from my analysis of the v4.2 training and inference paths): the v4.2 `dwell-time feature` accumulates dwell at every stop that shares a dock with a previous stop in the same route. When two stops reference the same dock door, the dwell from the shared window is counted once for each stop, not once per door occupancy. The double count is small per stop but compounds across the route, which is why the error tracks stop count.

Why we missed it: the accuracy dashboard samples single-stop routes by default. Multi-stop accuracy was only checked in the offline eval set, and that set has few shared-dock sequences, so the regression did not reach the release gate.

Fix: the feature definition needs to change to deduplicate shared-dock occupancy, and the model needs a retrain on v4.2 data with the corrected feature. Target is late September, pending the retrain and eval results.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Shared-dock occupancy is counted once per door window in the `dwell-time feature`, with a unit test covering two, three and five stops sharing one dock.
- Offline eval includes a stratified slice of `multi-stop routes` (2 to 8 stops, at least 30% shared-dock sequences).
- Mean absolute error on the final stop of routes with four or more stops returns to within the v4.1 baseline.
- Accuracy dashboard reports stratified metrics by stop count, not only single-stop routes.
- Customers in NS-4871 and NS-4955 are notified of the fix and the expected timeline by Customer Success before the retrain ships.

**Summary:** TRK-2268: Follow-up: rate limiter per carrier integration

**Description**

**Context**

The rate limiter shipped with the parent change last sprint fixed the worst burst behavior, but carrier integrations that poll telematics feeds are still hitting upstream quota limits during the morning dispatch window (roughly 05:00 to 08:00 local). When a 429 comes back, the gateway retries with a flat backoff. Retries from the same carrier stack on top of each other, which makes the throttling worse. Most of the 429s over the last two weeks came from three carriers, each with more than one active integration.

**Problem**

The token bucket is keyed per integration, not per carrier account. A carrier running a separate ELD feed and a yard feed gets two buckets, so its combined traffic can exceed the feed provider's per-account quota even though each bucket looks healthy on its own.

**Proposed change**

- Key the token bucket on carrier account ID, so all integrations for one account share a bucket.
- Replace the flat backoff with exponential backoff and jitter, capped at 60 seconds.
- Honor the `Retry-After` header when the upstream sends one. Never retry sooner than that value.
- Emit a metric per carrier account for throttled requests.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Carriers with two or more integrations share one bucket. Combined request rate never exceeds the configured quota in the staging load test.
- [ ] A 429 triggers exponential backoff with jitter. No retry fires before the `Retry-After` value.
- [ ] The ingestion dashboard shows throttled request counts per carrier account at 5-minute granularity.
- [ ] Replaying last morning-window traffic from staging produces zero dropped position updates for the Track test set.
- [ ] Single-integration carriers show no change in p95 ingestion latency (within 10%).

**Out of scope**

Changes to upstream vendor quotas. Predict ETA feature pipeline changes.

Messages from those devices are received at the edge but are not being written to the position stream for a window of time, then arrive in a batch. 3. Observe the live map view for the test trucks.
4. Expected: positions update within 60 seconds of the device report.
5. Actual: positions freeze for 2 to 4 minutes, then jump several blocks at once.

Reproduced on staging with latency injection. Not yet reproduced without injected latency, so we still need to confirm whether Brackenfield's real network path produces comparable delays.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Positions from the affected feed appear in the live map within 60 seconds of device report under the reproduction conditions above.

**Description**

Engineering issue TRK-2283 was opened from support ticket NS-4505, raised by Ironbark Fleet Services. Their dispatch team reports that Northstar Track is creating duplicate shipment records for the same load. Each duplicate carries its own ETA and fires its own arrival notification, so dispatchers see two entries for one truck and one delivery. Ironbark's dispatch lead says this has pushed three dock appointments into conflicting slots at their Midwest warehouses.

From the logs attached to NS-4505, the pattern looks like this: when a truck's telematics feed drops and reconnects, the ELD provider replays buffered position events with new message IDs. Our ingestion layer deduplicates on message ID, so the replayed events pass through as new. The shipment matcher then treats the first event after reconnect as an unmatched load and opens a second shipment record.

**Reproduction steps**

1. Create a shipment for a test truck with one pickup and one drop stop.
2. Start position events from the simulated ELD feed.
3. Pause the feed for 3 minutes, then resume it with the buffered events replayed under new message IDs.
4. Open the shipment list filtered to the test truck.
5. Expected: one active shipment. Actual: two active shipments with the same stop sequence.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Replayed position events from a reconnect do not create new shipment records.
- The matcher deduplicates on truck, timestamp window and stop sequence, not message ID alone.
- Existing duplicate shipments for Ironbark Fleet Services are merged by a one-time script, with an audit log entry for each merge.
- Regression test added to the ingestion suite covering the replay case.
- Predict ETA notifications are not re-sent for merged shipments.

**Estimate and owner**

Emeka Borowski owns the fix. Estimate is 5 points, covering the matcher change, the merge script and the regression test. The merge script needs a dry run against Ironbark's data before anything is written.

**Description**

*Context*

Northstar Track pulls position and status data from carrier telematics feeds. Each carrier integration currently shares one global request budget in the ingest worker pool. When one carrier's upstream API returns a burst of retries, the shared budget drains and healthy carriers see stale positions. Last week, a single fleet's feed backoff delayed live truck positions for two other carriers by roughly 14 minutes, which pushed Predict ETA outputs for their stops out of tolerance. Support received three tickets about it.

We need a rate limiter scoped per carrier integration, so that one feed's behavior cannot starve the others.

*Scope*

- Token-bucket limiter keyed by carrier integration ID, configurable per integration.
- Default limits come from the integration's contract tier and are stored in the integration config table.
- Limiter state lives in the shared cache so that all ingest workers enforce the same budget.
- Exceeded requests are queued with a bounded depth. Overflow is dropped and logged with the carrier ID.
- Metrics emitted per carrier: requests admitted, requests queued, requests dropped, current bucket level.

*Out of scope*

- Changes to the ELD vendor adapters themselves.
- Dock Scheduler polling, which uses a separate path.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. A simulated burst from one carrier at 10x its limit does not reduce admitted throughput for any other carrier by more than 5% in the load test.
2. Each integration's limit can be changed through the config table without a deploy, and takes effect within 60 seconds.
3. Queue depth never exceeds the configured bound; overflow produces a log line containing the carrier ID and a dropped-request counter increment.
4. The per-carrier metrics appear on the ingest dashboard and are tagged with the integration ID.
5. Under normal load (no carrier above its limit), p95 ingest latency is unchanged from the July baseline within measurement noise.
6. Runbook section for "carrier throttled" is updated and reviewed by Support Tier 2.

**Owner and status**

Lucia Berglund owns the design and the cache-backed limiter. Theo Strand owns the load test plan and acceptance verification. Status is In Progress: the limiter core is merged behind a feature flag, and the load harness is being built. Config table migration is not yet started.

# Release notes: Northstar Track 9.3

**Author:** Freya Alvarado, IT Administrator
**Published:** August 25, 2026, 09:20 UTC
**Product:** Northstar Track
**Audience:** Customer administrators, dispatch leads, and Northstar Support

## Overview

Track 9.3 adds shareable tracking links for consignees and speeds up map loading across the fleet view and the shipment detail page. Both changes are available to all Northstar Track accounts on the 9.x line. No action is required to receive them, but administrators should review the new sharing permissions before enabling links for their teams.

## What's new

### Shareable tracking links

Dispatchers and account administrators can now generate a tracking link for any active shipment and send it to a consignee, a receiving dock, or a customer contact who does not have a Northstar login. The link opens a read-only view showing the truck's current position, the predicted arrival time for the next stop, and the shipment status.

Key details:

- Links are created from the shipment detail page using the **Share tracking** action.
- Each link is tied to one shipment and expires automatically when the shipment is marked delivered, or after 7 days, whichever comes first.
- Administrators can revoke a link at any time from the shipment's sharing panel. Revoked links stop working immediately.
- Shared views show location and ETA only. Driver names, phone numbers, and vehicle telemetry are hidden by default.
- Each link view is logged in the shipment activity history with a timestamp and a coarse region, so dispatch can see when a consignee has checked.

Administrators control whether the feature is available to their users. It is off by default for accounts created before this release and must be turned on under **Settings > Sharing**.

### Faster map loading

The map component has been rebuilt to reduce time to first render on fleet views with more than 200 active trucks. In internal testing on large fleets, the fleet overview now draws its first frame noticeably faster, and panning and zooming no longer stall while live position updates arrive. Shipment detail maps also load their route layer before the full tile set, so the truck and next stop appear first.

No configuration changes are needed. Users on slower connections may see tiles appear progressively rather than all at once.

## Fixes

- Fixed an issue where the fleet overview could show a truck at its previous position for up to a minute after an ELD feed reconnected.
- Fixed a timezone display error in the arrival window tooltip for shipments crossing a daylight saving boundary.
- Corrected the export of dock appointment references in CSV downloads, which previously dropped leading zeros.

## Known limitations

- Shareable tracking links do not yet work for shipments that use manual location entry instead of a telematics feed. This is planned for a later release.
- Consignees opening a link on very old mobile browsers may see the map without the route layer. The status and ETA information still appear.
- Link analytics are limited to view counts in this release. Richer reporting is on the roadmap.

## Upgrade notes

Track 9.3 rolls out automatically to all accounts over the coming days. Customers on a pinned release channel will receive it when their channel is next updated. Administrators who want to test sharing before it reaches their users can enable it for a single pilot group first.

Please review your consignee communication guidelines before enabling shareable tracking links. Links carry the shipment reference, so treat them like any other external document.

## Questions

For rollout questions, contact your Northstar Customer Success Manager. For technical issues, open a ticket through the Northstar Support portal and mention Track 9.3 in the subject line.

**Description**

*Context*

Dock Scheduler currently accepts appointment requests against a warehouse as a whole. Any carrier with a valid account can book any dock door at any time that has capacity. Warehouse operators have asked for finer control. Dispatch teams at several multi-site fleet customers want certain doors reserved for specific carriers, for example temperature-controlled doors that only a contracted reefer carrier should use, or doors near a cross-dock lane that only one partner's trailers can fit.

Last quarter a customer's dispatch team reported that a non-contracted carrier had booked a refrigerated door during a peak window, which forced a reschedule for three loads. The customer has asked for a rule-based way to prevent this without manually editing the schedule each morning.

*Proposal*

Add an optional allow-list of carrier IDs per dock door. Each door can have zero or more rules. A door with no rules stays open to all carriers, which keeps current behavior unchanged. Rules are evaluated at booking time and again when a booking is moved.

*Acceptance criteria*

- Warehouse admins can create, edit and delete a carrier allow-list on any door from the dock configuration page.
- A booking request from a carrier not on a door's allow-list is rejected for that door with reason code `DOOR_CARRIER_RESTRICTED`. The request may still be offered other open doors the carrier is permitted to use.
- Doors with no allow-list behave exactly as they do today. Existing bookings are not invalidated when a rule is added; they are flagged in the admin view for review.
- Rule changes take effect within 60 seconds across all booking surfaces, including the carrier portal and the API.
- The REST API exposes the allow-list on the door resource and accepts updates with the same validation as the UI.
- Audit log entries record who changed a door's allow-list and the previous value.
- Load test: rule evaluation adds no more than 15 ms at p95 for a warehouse with 200 doors.

*Out of scope*

Time-of-day rules, load-type rules and per-carrier capacity caps are tracked separately in DOCK-671 and are not part of this issue.

**PRED-1324: Shadow evaluation for model releases**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Key | PRED-1324 |
| Type | Story |
| Priority | High |
| Status | In Progress |
| Assignee | Astrid Fujimoto |
| Reporter | Noa Yeboah |
| Component | Predict ETA |
| Labels | model-release, evaluation, ETA-accuracy |

**Description**

**Context**

Predict ETA currently promotes a new arrival-time model to production after offline validation on the holdout set and a canary on 5% of trucks. Last week's canary for the stop-level model passed offline metrics, but the live mean absolute error for multi-stop routes with dock appointments came in higher than the holdout suggested. The gap was traced to feature drift in dwell-time inputs that the holdout set does not represent well.

We need a way to run a candidate model in shadow against live traffic, scoring every stop it would have predicted without returning those predictions to customers. Shadow results should be compared against the production model and against actual arrival times once they land, so we catch regressions before any customer sees them.

This ticket covers the evaluation harness, the comparison report, and the release gate. It does not cover retraining pipelines or changes to the dock-scheduling feature store, which are tracked separately.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. Every candidate model version receives a copy of each live prediction request for at least 72 hours before promotion is eligible.
2. Shadow predictions are written to a separate store and are never returned through the public API or the customer dashboard.
3. A nightly job computes MAE, median absolute error, and the 90th-percentile error per stop type (linehaul, pickup, delivery, dock-appointment) for both the candidate and the production model, joined against recorded arrival events.
4. Results are broken out by customer account and by route length bucket, so a regression affecting one fleet cannot be hidden by aggregate numbers.
5. The release gate blocks promotion if the candidate's MAE on dock-appointment stops is more than 3% worse than production in any account with at least 500 scored stops.
6. The gate can be overridden only by a named approver in Product, with the reason recorded on the release ticket.
7. Shadow traffic adds no more than 5% to p95 latency on the prediction endpoint, verified under load in staging.
8. Runbook documents how to enable shadowing for a candidate, how to read the report, and how to disable it during an incident.

**Out of scope**

Changes to the feature store, retraining cadence, and customer-facing accuracy reporting.

---

**Comments**

**Noa Yeboah, 2026-08-27 08:59 UTC**
Opened this after the canary review. The holdout set clearly underweights the dwell-time distribution we're seeing on the newer carrier integrations. Astrid, can you take the harness design? I'd like the nightly job to run on the existing analytics cluster so we don't provision anything new.

**Astrid Fujimoto**
Yes, I'll take it. Plan is to fan out at the ingestion layer so shadow scoring never sits on the request path. That should keep the latency budget in AC 7 comfortable. One question: do we want the candidate scored against the same feature snapshot as production, or its own? I'd argue same snapshot, otherwise we're comparing feature pipelines as well as models.

**Oskar Thorsby**
Same snapshot. If the candidate needs a different feature version, that's a separate ticket and it should block promotion anyway. Also, please log the model hash alongside every shadow record. We got bitten last quarter by two candidates with the same version string.

**Leila Haddad**

# Release Notes: Dock Scheduler 4.1

**Released:** August 29, 2026
**Author:** Kalani Fenwick, Support Engineer, Northstar Systems
**Applies to:** All Dock Scheduler accounts on the hosted platform

## Overview

Dock Scheduler 4.1 adds two capabilities to appointment booking and yard flow. The first is detection of **carrier no-show** patterns, so warehouse planners can see which carriers repeatedly miss booked dock slots before those misses disrupt the day. The second is a waitlist for cancelled slots, which lets carriers and dispatchers claim an opening without phoning the warehouse.

Both features are on by default for accounts on the Dock Scheduler plan. Administrators can change the settings described below from the site configuration page.

## What's new

### Carrier no-show flagging

Dock Scheduler now tracks each booked appointment through to arrival. An appointment counts as a no-show when the carrier has not checked in within the grace window after the booked start time. The grace window defaults to 30 minutes and can be set between 15 and 90 minutes per site.

When a carrier accumulates no-shows above a threshold within a rolling 30-day period, the carrier is flagged on the Carriers tab. The flag shows:

- The number of no-shows in the window and the number of total bookings
- The most common booked time block for the misses
- The last three appointments with their outcome

The default threshold is three no-shows, or a no-show rate above 20 percent for carriers with at least ten bookings. Both values are configurable.

Flags do not block bookings. They are advisory and appear as a warning when a planner books a flagged carrier. Carriers do not see the flag.

### Waitlist for cancelled slots

When an appointment is cancelled, the freed slot is offered to the waitlist in the order requests were received. Carriers join the waitlist from the booking portal by selecting "Join waitlist" on a fully booked day. They receive an email when a matching slot opens, and the first carrier to confirm holds the slot.

Planners can see the waitlist for each dock door and manually assign a slot to a waitlisted carrier. Waitlist entries expire at the end of the booking day.

Waitlist offers are sent only to carriers whose equipment type and trailer length match the dock door.

## Changes and fixes

- Yard flow view now refreshes every 60 seconds instead of every five minutes.
- Appointment export includes the cancellation reason when one was entered.
- Fixed a case where a rescheduled appointment kept the original dock door assignment in the daily summary.
- Fixed a timezone issue that shifted some appointments by one hour for sites in regions observing daylight saving time.

## Upgrade notes

No action is required for most accounts. Dock Scheduler 4.1 applies the default no-show settings to all sites on upload. Accounts that already use custom booking rules should review the new grace window setting under Site Settings > Appointments before the next busy period, since the default may differ from what the site used before.

Existing carrier records are scanned once during the upgrade to build their no-show history. The scan uses only appointments from the past 30 days. Older data is not imported.

## Known limitations

- The waitlist does not support multi-door appointments. Those must be booked manually.
- No-show detection depends on check-in events from the carrier's gate or yard system. Sites without a check-in integration will see no-show flags only when planners mark arrivals manually.
- Waitlist emails are sent in the language set on the carrier profile. Templates are currently available in English and Norwegian.

## Support

For questions about these features, contact Support through the usual channel. Escalations involving a carrier dispute over a no-show flag should be routed to Customer Success so the account team can review the history with the customer.

# Implementation Checklist

**Author:** Astrid Ulrich, Support Specialist, Northstar Systems
**Date:** August 30, 2026, 12:00 UTC
**Status:** Working draft

## Purpose

This checklist covers the steps from kickoff to go-live sign-off for a new fleet customer deploying Northstar Track, Predict ETA, and Dock Scheduler. Support owns the checklist. Customer Success (Arjun Chaudry) owns the customer relationship, and Engineering owns any feed or model configuration. Each item lists an owner and a done condition. Mark items complete in the shared tracker, not in this document.

## 1. Kickoff (Week 1)

- [ ] Confirm the customer's signed order form and the product set (Track, Predict ETA, Dock Scheduler, or a combination).
- [ ] Record the customer's executive sponsor, operations lead, dispatch lead, and IT contact. Do not proceed until all four names are in the account record.
- [ ] Collect the list of trucks and telematics providers by fleet segment. Note any fleet that uses a non-standard ELD export.
- [ ] Hold the kickoff call. Agree on the target go-live window and the escalation path to Support Lead, Tier 2 (Noa Segal).

## 2. Data Access and Feeds (Weeks 1 to 2)

- [ ] Request read-only feed credentials from the customer's IT team. Confirm the scope in writing before any credentials are shared.
- [ ] Validate the first 24 hours of location pings for each truck. Flag trucks reporting fewer than one ping every five minutes.
- [ ] Confirm time zone and unit settings for each depot.
- [ ] Engineering (Emeka Ibekwe) confirms that stop data imports cleanly for at least one full route day.

## 3. Pilot Depot Selection

Choose one **pilot depot** before any other depot is configured. A good pilot depot has:

- A dispatch team willing to give feedback twice a week during the pilot.
- Stable routes with at least 20 stops per day, so Predict ETA has enough history to show a useful signal.
- Dock appointments that already sit in a system we can read, or a manual process the dock supervisor will keep current during the pilot.
- No planned facility changes during the pilot window.

Record the chosen depot, the reasons for the choice, and the two depots kept as backups. Ingrid Solberg's dispatch team at Halvorsen Freight Group is the reference for dispatch-side criteria. Any customer can name its own pilot depot; the checklist does not assume a specific account.

- [ ] Pilot depot named and approved by the customer operations lead.
- [ ] Two backup depots recorded.

## 4. Dispatcher Training

- [ ] Schedule two 60-minute sessions for dispatchers at the pilot depot, one before go-live and one at the end of week one.
- [ ] Walk through the live tracking view, the ETA confidence band, and how to report a wrong prediction.
- [ ] For Dock Scheduler users, cover appointment creation, rescheduling, and yard flow status.
- [ ] Collect a signed attendance list and send the recording and quick-reference card within one business day.
- [ ] Leila Haddad (Product) reviews the feedback from the first training session for anything that affects ETA model presentation.

## 5. Pilot Operation (Weeks 3 to 4)

- [ ] Daily check of prediction accuracy for the pilot depot. Oskar Thorsby (Staff ML Engineer) reviews any stop with an error over the agreed threshold.
- [ ] Twice-weekly call with the customer operations lead. Keep notes in the account record.
- [ ] Log every support ticket from the pilot depot with a tag for `pilot`.
- [ ] Decide at the end of week four whether to expand to the remaining depots.

## 6. Rollout to Remaining Depots

- [ ] Repeat steps 2 and 4 for each depot.
- [ ] Confirm that every depot has a named dispatch lead in the account record.
- [ ] Customer Success confirms that no depot is still on a manual process without a documented reason.

## 7. Go-Live Sign-Off

The **go-live sign-off** happens only when all of the following are true:

- [ ] Every depot in scope is live and has completed at least five working days without a Severity 1 or Severity 2 ticket.
- [ ] The customer operations lead and the dispatch lead have each signed the acceptance note.
- [ ] Open tickets are either resolved or assigned a dated fix in the tracker.
- [ ] Customer Success has recorded the handoff to the ongoing support plan.

Support Lead, Tier 2 approves the sign-off in the tracker. Customer Success sends the acceptance note to the customer's executive sponsor the same day.

## Open Questions

- Whether the standard feed credential template covers the newest ELD export format used by two fleet segments.
- Whether Dock Scheduler should go live in the same window as Track, or one week later.

**Key:** TRK-2303
**Type:** Bug
**Priority:** High
**Status:** In Progress
**Assignee:** Dara Sandoval
**Reporter:** Mira Ingram
**Component:** Track / Ingestion
**Created:** August 30, 2026, 18:15 UTC

**Summary:** Duplicate shipment detection on TMS retries

**Description**

Some customer transportation management systems (TMS) retry shipment update webhooks when they do not receive a timely acknowledgment from us. Our ingestion layer currently treats each retried payload as a new shipment when the retry arrives with a different delivery attempt ID but the same shipment reference and stop sequence. This creates duplicate shipment records in Northstar Track, which then show up as phantom trucks on the live map and inflate per-truck billing counts for Predict ETA and Dock Scheduler.

Three accounts reported this over the last two weeks. Halvorsen Freight Group's dispatch team noticed two identical lanes on the same tractor and raised it through their account contact. The duplicates are not dropped by our existing idempotency check because that check keys on the full payload hash, and the TMS adds a retry timestamp to each attempt.

**Context**

- The idempotency key is currently derived from the raw payload hash (see `ingest/normalize.py`).
- The retry timestamp and the TMS-side attempt counter are both inside the hashed body, so retries never collide.
- Billing reads from the active shipment table, so duplicates count toward truck totals.

**Acceptance Criteria**

1. Retried shipment updates with the same shipment reference, stop sequence, and carrier identifier are recognized as duplicates and do not create a new shipment record.
2. Idempotency key excludes retry timestamp and attempt counter fields; the key is built from a documented set of business fields.
3. When a duplicate is detected, the newest non-null field values are merged into the existing record and the event is logged with the original delivery attempt ID.
4. Existing duplicate records created since the regression are identified by a one-off query and listed for review by Customer Success before any deletion.
5. No change to billing counts for accounts without duplicates; a before-and-after billing reconciliation is attached to the release ticket.
6. Unit tests cover retry sequences with 1, 3, and 10 attempts, plus out-of-order delivery.

**Comments**

**Dara Sandoval:** Drafted the key change behind a flag. The business-field list needs a review from Oskar because the stop sequence can be renumbered after a reroute. If it is renumbered, we might miss a legitimate new stop. I want his read before we merge.

**Mira Ingram:** Agreed on the reroute case. Let's treat a renumbered stop as a new stop only if the stop coordinates also change by more than the geofence radius. Please add that to the tests. I'd also like the merge logic to leave the original record's created timestamp untouched.

**Dara Sandoval:** Done. Added the geofence check and a test for reroute with renumbering. Billing reconciliation query is running against the staging copy now.

**Mira Ingram:** Good. Once the reconciliation matches, move this to Ready for Review. Noa should be told so Support can answer the Halvorsen ticket once the fix is deployed. Not going to promise a deploy date in that ticket until the query results are back.

**TRK-2307: Customer escalation: stale map tiles**

**Key:** TRK-2307
**Type:** Bug
**Priority:** High
**Status:** In Progress
**Assignee:** Sana Corbett
**Reporter:** Sana Corbett
**Component:** Northstar Track / Map Rendering
**Estimate:** 5 story points (about 3 engineering days)
**Customer account:** Riverstone Haulage (beverage distribution, DACH, 1,300 trucks)
**Linked support ticket:** NS-4564
**Products affected:** Northstar Track, Predict ETA, Dock Scheduler

---

### Description

Riverstone Haulage's dispatch team reported through support ticket NS-4564 that the live map in the Track console sometimes shows truck positions over roads and yards that have changed since the map was last drawn. Dispatchers have seen trucks appear to drive through a closed road segment, and at least one yard entrance is drawn in the wrong place after a re-layout. The customer's operations lead said this has led to two drivers being sent to the wrong gate last week.

Truck positions themselves look correct in the telematics feed. The problem is in the base map layer. Tiles cached by our map rendering service are served well past their intended lifetime, and the tile refresh job does not invalidate tiles for regions where the upstream provider has published an update. Riverstone's depots are concentrated in regions with frequent road changes, so the problem is more visible for them than for most accounts.

Elif Petrakis has agreed that this is a customer-facing correctness issue and should be handled ahead of the planned rendering refactor.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Log in to a tenant with at least one fleet in a region that had map updates in the past month (use the staging tenant seeded with the DACH dataset).
2. Open the live map and pan to a depot whose surrounding roads were updated upstream.
3. Compare the rendered base layer with the current upstream tile for the same zoom level and coordinates.
4. Observe that the cached tile still shows the old road geometry. Tile metadata shows a `cached_at` timestamp older than the refresh threshold, but no invalidation event was recorded.
5. Trigger the nightly tile refresh manually. Confirm the stale tile is not replaced, because the refresh job only checks tiles that have expired by age, not tiles flagged by upstream version changes.

### Root cause (preliminary)

The refresh job keys off `expires_at` only. The upstream version header, which the provider uses to signal regional updates, is read at fetch time but never stored. As a result, a tile fetched before an upstream change can remain valid in our cache for the full TTL even when the source has changed.

### Acceptance criteria

- Tiles are invalidated when the upstream version header for their region changes, not only when they expire by age.
- The staging reproduction in steps 1 to 5 shows the updated geometry within one refresh cycle.
- Regression tests cover a changed tile, an unchanged tile, and a tile whose version header is missing.
- Cache hit rate in staging does not drop by more than 5 percent after the change.
- Riverstone Haulage confirms through NS-4564 that the affected depots render correctly.

### Out of scope

- Changes to the upstream provider's update cadence.
- Rendering performance work tracked separately.

# Security Questionnaire Standard Answers

**Owner:** Sales Development, with review by Engineering and Legal
**Last updated:** August 31, 2026
**Author:** Farid Popescu, Sales Development Representative

## Purpose

This page holds approved answers for the security sections of customer and prospect questionnaires. Use these answers as written. If a question falls outside this page, or the customer's wording asks for something more specific, send it to the Security queue in the usual way and do not improvise an answer. Reps should not promise roadmap items or contractual commitments that are not listed here.

## Independent Assurance

**Q: Do you have an independent audit report for your controls?**

Yes. Northstar Systems maintains a SOC 2 Type II report covering the security, availability, and confidentiality criteria for the Northstar Track, Predict ETA, and Dock Scheduler products. The report is issued by an independent auditor and covers an observation period of at least six months. The current report is available under NDA through the Trust page. Bridge letters are available on request for periods between report issuances.

Do not describe the report as a "certification." The correct term is "SOC 2 Type II report."

## Data Location and Residency

**Q: Where is customer data stored?**

Customer data is hosted in our primary region in North America by default. An **EU data residency** option is available for accounts that require customer shipment, telemetry, and stop data to be stored and processed within the European Union. EU data residency is set at the account level during onboarding and applies to primary storage, backups, and logs that contain personal data.

Some operational metadata, such as aggregate platform health metrics, is processed outside the EU. Legal has approved the wording for this exception and it is included in the Data Processing Addendum. If a customer asks for a complete list of sub-processors by region, refer them to the current sub-processor list on the Trust page.

Do not promise EU data residency for accounts that were provisioned before the option was enabled. Those accounts require a migration, which is scoped separately by Operations.

## Identity and Access

**Q: Do you support single sign-on?**

Yes. Northstar supports SAML 2.0 and OpenID Connect single sign-on with common identity providers. SSO enforcement can be set per organization, and administrators can require SSO for all users in their tenant.

**Q: Do you support automated user provisioning?**

Yes. SCIM 2.0 provisioning is available for user creation, attribute updates, group mapping, and deactivation. Deprovisioning through SCIM takes effect within minutes of the change in the customer's identity provider.

**Q: Do you support role-based access control?**

Yes. Roles are scoped to the organization, to individual sites or yards, and to Dock Scheduler appointment calendars. Audit logs record role changes and administrative actions.

## Encryption and Infrastructure

**Q: How is data encrypted?**

Data is encrypted in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher. Data at rest is encrypted using AES-256. Encryption keys are managed by the cloud provider's key management service with rotation enforced on a fixed schedule.

**Q: Do you perform penetration testing?**

Yes. Third-party penetration tests are run at least annually, and results are summarized in the Trust page. Customers may request the executive summary under NDA.

## Incident Response

**Q: What is your breach notification commitment?**

Northstar notifies affected customers without undue delay after confirming a security incident that affects their data. Specific timelines in the Data Processing Addendum take precedence over any general statement in this page.

## Escalation

For any question not covered here, or for any request to modify these answers, contact the Security queue. Do not send unreviewed documents, architecture diagrams, or policy text to a prospect without Legal approval.

**Description**

**Context**

The shipment timeline view in Northstar Track renders every position event, geofence crossing and status change for a shipment as a single list. For long-haul shipments with dense telematics feeds, a single timeline can hold several thousand rows. Last quarter we shipped a first pass at virtualization on the web client (TRK-2291), which limited DOM nodes to the visible window. That fixed the worst render freezes, but the timeline API still returns the full event history on every load, and the client still holds all of it in memory.

This ticket covers the follow-up: paging the timeline endpoint and making the client request only the window it needs. Two customers on the Halvorsen Freight Group account reported slow loads on shipments with more than 4,000 events. Their dispatch team opens these timelines during live exceptions, so the delay matters.

**Scope**

- Add cursor-based paging to the timeline endpoint, keyed on event sequence number.
- Return a stable `next_cursor` and a `has_more` flag in each response.
- Update the web client to fetch the window around the current scroll position and prefetch one page ahead in each direction.
- Keep the existing full-history export working for the CSV download. It should stream from the export path, not from the paged endpoint.

**Out of scope**

- Changes to how Predict ETA consumes timeline events. Leila Haddad's team has confirmed the ETA pipeline reads from the event store directly.
- Mobile client.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. Timeline endpoint accepts `cursor` and `limit` parameters. Default `limit` is 200, maximum is 500.
2. Responses are stable across concurrent event writes: a cursor returned earlier never skips or duplicates events that were present when it was issued.
3. On a 4,000-event shipment, first meaningful paint of the timeline is under 1.5 seconds at p95 in staging.
4. Scrolling to any position in a 10,000-event shipment does not trigger a fetch of more than two pages at once.
5. CSV export produces byte-identical output to the pre-change export for the same shipment fixtures.
6. Existing timeline integration tests pass unchanged, except for tests that assert on full-list length, which are updated to assert on the first page.
7. Feature flag `timeline_paging` gates the new behavior per account, defaulting to off.

**Owner and status**

Ilse owns the API and paging design. Rina owns the event-store query work and the staging benchmarks. Status is In Progress: the cursor design is agreed, and the query plan review is done. The client work starts once the endpoint is merged behind the flag.

**PRED-1329: Follow-up: refresh eta within two minutes of reroute**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Key | PRED-1329 |
| Type | Bug (Follow-up) |
| Priority | High |
| Status | In Progress |
| Assignee | Gideon Lundgren |
| Reporter | Nadia Echeverria |
| Component | Predict ETA / Streaming Pipeline |
| Created | September 3, 2026, 07:54 UTC |

**Description**

Follow-up to the reroute incident reviewed last week. When a truck is rerouted mid-trip, the predicted arrival time for downstream stops in Predict ETA can remain on the pre-reroute path for longer than the two-minute target. Dispatchers at customer sites, including Halvorsen Freight Group's dispatch team, reported stale arrival windows on Track and Dock Scheduler appointments after reroutes were accepted in the telematics feed.

Root cause from the first pass: the reroute event is ingested and stored, but the ETA recompute job only triggers on the next scheduled position update. On trucks reporting at lower frequency, that gap can exceed the target. The fix in PRED-1329's parent change added an event-driven trigger, but it has not been verified end to end under load.

**Acceptance criteria**

- A reroute event from the telematics feed triggers an ETA recompute for every remaining stop on the affected trip.
- Refreshed ETAs are visible in Track and written to Dock Scheduler appointment windows within two minutes of the reroute event timestamp, measured at the 95th percentile over a one-week window in staging.
- Trips with no subsequent position update still recompute on the reroute event.
- Duplicate reroute events for the same trip within a 30-second window do not produce duplicate recomputes.
- Recompute failures emit an alert to the on-call channel and do not silently keep the old ETA.

**TRK-2323: Shareable tracking link expiry**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Key | TRK-2323 |
| Type | Story |
| Priority | High |
| Status | In Progress |
| Assignee | Dalia Hayashi |
| Reporter | Arjun Chaudry |
| Component | Northstar Track / Shared Links |
| Labels | customer-facing, security-review |
| Created | September 3, 2026, 12:07 UTC |

**Description**

**Context**

Northstar Track lets fleet customers generate a shareable tracking link for a shipment or truck. Dispatchers send these links to consignees, brokers and subcontracted carriers so they can follow a delivery without a Northstar login. Today the links never expire. Once generated, a link returns live position, predicted stop times (from Predict ETA) and the consignee-facing status page until someone manually revokes it.

Two customers raised this during their quarterly reviews. Halvorsen Freight Group's dispatch team (Ingrid Solberg's group) pointed out that links sent for completed loads remain active indefinitely, and their procurement team (Lars Eskeland) asked whether links can be time-boxed to match contract windows. Their security questionnaire marks indefinite access as a finding. Tobias Brandvold asked for the same behavior across all accounts, not just theirs.

**Proposed behavior**

Add an optional expiry to shareable links:

- Default expiry is 72 hours after the shipment's last recorded event, not after link creation. A load that is still moving should never lose its link.
- Dispatchers can choose a custom expiry at creation time, from 1 hour up to 30 days.
- When a link expires, the page shows a neutral "This tracking link has expired" message with the sending company's contact name. No position data is returned.
- Existing links are not changed by this release. They get the no-expiry behavior until a customer opts in through the admin settings.

**Out of scope**

- Changes to the ELD or telematics ingestion path.
- Per-recipient access controls or passcodes. These are tracked separately.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. A new link created with default settings expires 72 hours after the latest event on its shipment, and the expiry time is stored on the link record.
2. A link created with a custom expiry between 1 hour and 30 days expires at that time, and the value is validated server-side. Values outside the range are rejected with a clear error.
3. An expired link returns the expired page with HTTP 410 and does not return any position, ETA or stop data.
4. Expiry is evaluated against the server clock in UTC. A link never expires while its shipment shows new events within the window.
5. Dispatchers can extend or revoke a link from the shipment screen. Extending a link writes an audit entry with the user and the new expiry.
6. Existing links are unchanged on deploy. A feature flag controls the new default per account.
7. Unit and integration tests cover the expiry boundary, the event-driven reset, and the 410 response.

**Notes**

Security review (flagged under the security-review label) must sign off on the 410 response body before merge. Lucia has the checklist.

---

# Quarterly planning notes: Q3 2026

**Author:** Adrian Bakshi (Support Engineer, Northstar Systems)
**Date:** September 5, 2026, 07:41 UTC

## Purpose

These notes capture the Q3 2026 bets as discussed in planning and summarize what support has been seeing that informed them. They are a working record, not a commitment. Owners should confirm scope with their leads before next quarter's plan is locked.

## Q3 bets

We agreed on three bets for the quarter:

1. **Predict ETA multi-stop accuracy.** Single-stop predictions are performing well for most accounts. Multi-stop routes, where a truck has four or more stops, are where customers are escalating. Leila Haddad owns the product side, and Oskar Thorsby is scoping the model changes.
2. **Dock Scheduler self-serve onboarding.** Today, most Dock Scheduler setups require a Customer Success engagement before the first appointment can be booked. That slows activation and makes the product look heavier than it is. The goal is a setup path a warehouse admin can finish without help.
3. **EMEA expansion.** Henrik Dahlgren is leading the regional push. Support will need to staff coverage for European business hours and document the regional escalation path before the first wave of new accounts goes live.

## What support is seeing

Over the last several weeks, the Tier 2 queue has been dominated by ETA complaints. Most of them share a pattern: the prediction looks reasonable for the first stop and drifts later in the route. Customers describe the drift as "confident and wrong," which is worse than an obvious gap because dispatch trusts the number and reschedules receiving teams around it.

Noa Segal's team tagged roughly a third of Tier 2 tickets in the last period as multi-stop related. Emeka Ibekwe has been reproducing a subset of these against recorded telematics feeds and found that the drift correlates with stops where the truck waits for a dock, not with drive-time error. That is useful for the model team and should be in the bet's problem statement.

On the Dock Scheduler side, onboarding tickets are mostly the same few questions: how to map existing dock doors to the yard layout, how to set appointment windows per carrier, and how to invite a second admin. None of these are hard, but each one currently needs a person. Arjun Chaudry has offered to pull the last quarter's onboarding transcripts so we can see where people stalled.

## Risks

- **Multi-stop scope creep.** The accuracy problem touches the feature pipeline, not only the model. If the fix needs new inputs from carriers, timelines will stretch. We should decide early whether the Q3 target is accuracy on existing inputs only.
- **Self-serve support load.** Removing the onboarding call may shift work into support tickets. We should set a threshold for how many setup tickets per week would signal the flow is failing.
- **EMEA coverage.** We have not yet confirmed staffing for the European hours. This is the least settled of the three bets.

## Open questions

- Who owns the decision on whether Predict ETA multi-stop changes ship behind a flag for a subset of accounts first?
- Does the self-serve Dock Scheduler flow need its own pricing or packaging review with Priya Kaplan before launch?
- Can Selin Yilmaz pull a clean baseline for multi-stop escalations so we can measure movement by end of quarter?

## Next steps

- Leila to draft the problem statement for multi-stop accuracy, including Emeka's dock-wait finding, by next review.
- Oskar to estimate the minimum viable model change and flag any new input dependencies.
- Support to list the top ten Dock Scheduler onboarding questions and mark which ones a setup wizard could answer.
- Henrik and Noa to agree on a draft EMEA escalation path.
- Revisit these bets at the next planning review.

# ELD Integration Guide

**Owner:** Uma Bastien, Customer Success Specialist
**Last updated:** September 10, 2026
**Audience:** ELD and telematics partners connecting feeds to Northstar Track and Predict ETA

## Purpose

This guide describes what Northstar Systems needs from an electronic logging device (ELD) or telematics partner before a fleet's trucks can appear in Northstar Track. It covers update cadence, gap recovery, and event identity. Partners that meet these requirements give customers accurate live positions and reliable arrival predictions. Partners that miss them cause stale tiles on the dispatch screen and degraded ETAs in Predict ETA, which customers notice quickly.

Questions about onboarding should go to your Northstar integration contact. Questions about a specific fleet's data should go through that fleet's Customer Success Manager.

## 1. Position update cadence

Each active vehicle must send a position record at least once every 30 seconds while the ignition is on. We call this the **30-second position** requirement.

- Records must include timestamp (UTC, millisecond precision), latitude, longitude, speed, heading, and odometer where available.
- Timestamps come from the device or the telematics platform's clock, not from the time of ingestion on our side.
- Stationary vehicles with the engine running still send a position every 30 seconds. Engine-off vehicles may send a single record on shutdown and then one every 15 minutes as a heartbeat.
- Do not batch positions into longer intervals to save bandwidth. Batching is acceptable only when the buffer is flushed within 60 seconds and timestamps stay accurate.

Predict ETA uses this cadence to estimate speed changes near stops. Gaps longer than two minutes reduce prediction confidence for the affected stops and are flagged in the customer's dashboard.

## 2. Backfill after gaps

Connectivity drops happen. When a vehicle's feed resumes after a gap, the partner must **backfill** the missed position records in timestamp order before sending live data.

- Backfill covers the full gap, up to 72 hours. Older gaps may be reported as a summary with a `gap_reason` code.
- Backfilled records keep their original timestamps. Do not re-stamp them with the time of delivery.
- Send backfill in chunks of no more than 500 records per request, and wait for acknowledgment before sending the next chunk.
- Live records that arrive during a backfill window should be queued behind the backfill, not interleaved with it.

Northstar will mark backfilled segments on the route history so dispatchers can see that a past position was reconstructed rather than observed live.

## 3. Idempotent event identifiers

Every event must carry a stable, globally unique `event_id`. Retries, replays, and backfills will send some events more than once, and we must be able to discard duplicates without losing data.

- Use a UUID v4 or a deterministic hash of `(device_id, timestamp, event_type)`.
- Re-sending an event with the same `event_id` must produce the same result on our side. We will accept it and ignore the duplicate.
- Never reuse an `event_id` for a different event, even after a device reset. A reset device must generate new identifiers.
- Event types we process today include position, engine state, hard braking, geofence entry and exit, and driver login.

## 4. Delivery and acknowledgment

- Use HTTPS with TLS 1.2 or higher.
- Our endpoint returns `202 Accepted` when events are queued and `409 Conflict` when an `event_id` was already processed with different content. Treat `409` as a bug report, not a retry signal, and contact your integration contact.
- Retries should use exponential backoff, starting at 5 seconds and capped at 5 minutes.

## 5. Testing before go-live

Before a fleet is enabled, the partner must pass three checks in our sandbox:

1. Sustained cadence test: 30 minutes of simulated position data at the 30-second position rate, with no missing intervals.
2. Backfill test: a simulated four-hour gap, followed by backfill in chunks, with timestamps verified in the route history view.
3. Duplicate test: every event sent twice, with duplicates confirmed as discarded.

**PRED-1339: Refresh ETA within two minutes of reroute**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Key | PRED-1339 |
| Type | Story |
| Priority | High |
| Status | In Progress |
| Assignee | Dalia Kerrigan |
| Reporter | Yara Rosales |
| Component | Predict ETA, ETA Pipeline |
| Labels | reroute, latency, halvorsen-escalation |
| Created | September 12, 2026, 08:40 UTC |

**Description**

*Context*

Predict ETA currently recalculates arrival times for a truck on a fixed cycle. When a dispatcher reroutes a truck, the new route can take several minutes to reach the predicted-arrival output that customers see in Northstar Track and in the Dock Scheduler appointment view. During that gap, the dock team sees an ETA for a route the truck is no longer running.

Halvorsen Freight Group raised this in their quarterly review. Their dispatch team, led by Ingrid Solberg, reports that appointment changes at receiving docks are made from the stale ETA and then have to be moved again. Tobias Brandvold has asked for the gap to be closed before their next peak season planning cycle. Lars Eskeland has linked the contract clause that makes this a service-level item for them.

Reroute events already arrive from the telematics feed as route-change messages. The gap is in how quickly those messages trigger a fresh prediction and how quickly the result is published.

*Scope*

- Trigger an ETA recalculation for every stop on a truck within a reroute event.
- Publish the refreshed ETA to the Track and Dock Scheduler read paths.
- Do not change the ML model itself. Oskar Thorsby has confirmed the existing model handles mid-route inputs; this issue only changes when it runs.

*Acceptance criteria*

1. A reroute event results in refreshed ETAs for all remaining stops within 120 seconds at the 95th percentile, measured from event receipt to published value.
2. ETAs for stops not affected by the reroute are not republished, to avoid noise in downstream dock appointment changes.
3. If the recalculation fails, the previous ETA remains visible and is flagged as stale in the API payload.
4. Duplicate route-change messages within a 30-second window produce one recalculation.
5. Dashboard panel "Reroute-to-publish latency" is added to the Predict ETA on-call board.
6. Runbook entry added by Theo Wexley before release.

*Out of scope*

Changes to the telematics vendor integration, changes to the dock appointment UI, and any new customer-facing setting.

Priority stays High. This is one of the two items on the Halvorsen escalation list for Q3. Dalia, can you confirm the 120-second target is realistic given the current batch window? If not, flag it today so Leila can talk to Halvorsen before their review.

**Dalia Kerrigan** — 10:02
Looked at the scheduler. The fixed cycle is the main cost. Event-driven trigger should get us under the target for most reroutes. Two concerns: burst load when a dispatcher reroutes a whole depot at once, and the dedupe window may hide a legitimate second reroute. I'll put a test for both in the branch and see what the p95 looks like on replayed traffic.

**Oskar Thorsby** — 11:37
Model side is fine for mid-route inputs. One note: if the reroute happens inside the last few kilometers, the feature set is thinner, so the confidence band will widen. That's expected. Please don't clamp the band to hide it, because downstream dock scheduling uses it.

**Dalia Kerrigan** — 14:20

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Key | DOCK-669 |
| Type | Bug |
| Priority | Highest |

| Assignee | Jonas Cervantes |
| Reporter | Noa Segal |

| Linked | NS-4722 (support ticket, Glenhaven Distribution) |
| Customer | Glenhaven Distribution (retail replenishment, Nordics, 1,780 trucks) |
| Products | Northstar Track, Predict ETA, Dock Scheduler |

**Description**

Escalated from support ticket NS-4722. Glenhaven Distribution reports that carriers using the self-booking flow in Dock Scheduler sometimes see an appointment confirmed in the portal, but the slot does not appear on the warehouse dock calendar. Their dispatch team then receives the arrival with no dock assigned, and trucks queue at the gate. Over the past two weeks, the customer has logged 31 such cases. Their operations lead has asked for a root-cause answer and a fix before next quarter's peak volume.

Predict ETA is also affected downstream. The arrival prediction for these stops uses the appointment time, so a missing booking leaves the stop without a planned slot and the ETA falls back to the raw telematics estimate.

**Reproduction steps**

1. Log in to the carrier portal as a carrier user on a Glenhaven Distribution account.
2. Open a dock slot that is within 30 minutes of an existing booking at the same door.
3. Submit the booking and wait for the confirmation screen.
4. Refresh the warehouse dock calendar. In roughly one in five attempts, the slot is missing.
5. Check the booking record. The status shows "confirmed" with no door ID.

Reproduced in staging on the 14th with a 30-minute buffer configured. Failure occurs only when two bookings are created within the same second on the same door, which suggests a race in the write path.

**Owner**

Jonas Cervantes (ML Engineer, Northstar Systems) owns the fix. Lucia Berglund (Site Reliability Engineer, Northstar Systems) is reviewing the write path and the retry behavior.

**Estimate**

Three engineering days for the fix and tests, plus one day for a staged rollout to the Glenhaven tenant.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Concurrent bookings on the same door never both return "confirmed"; one must be rejected with a clear message to the carrier.
- Every confirmed booking has a non-null door ID and appears on the dock calendar within 5 seconds.
- Predict ETA uses the confirmed appointment time for all stops with a booking.
- A regression test covers two simultaneous requests on one door.
- Glenhaven's 31 affected bookings are reconciled and listed in NS-4722 for their operations team.

**Comments**

**Lucia Berglund, 16 Sep, 14:12**
Pulled the write logs for the affected door. Both requests read the slot as free before either committed. The check and the insert aren't in one transaction. Adding a unique constraint on door plus start time should stop the double write. I'd still like the retry path reviewed before we ship.

**Jonas Cervantes, 16 Sep, 16:40**
Agreed on the constraint. I also found that the ETA service caches booking state for ten minutes, so Predict ETA may show a stale slot even after the fix lands. I'm adding a cache invalidation on booking events. Migration script is drafted, not yet run on staging.

**Noa Segal, 16 Sep, 17:05**
Glenhaven's operations lead wants a written update in NS-4722 today. Can you confirm whether the 31 cases can be reconciled from the logs, or do we need their carrier to resubmit?

**Jonas Cervantes, 16 Sep, 19:25**
Logs are enough for 28 of the 31. The other three were booked on a door that was later renamed, so I need Glenhaven's dock map to match them. I'll post the list in NS-4722 once the reconciliation script finishes.

**Key:** DOCK-680
**Type:** Task
**Priority:** Medium
**Status:** In Progress
**Assignee:** Astrid Fujimoto
**Reporter:** Mira Ingram
**Component:** Dock Scheduler / Reporting
**Summary:** Follow-up: no-show pattern report

---

**Description**

Follow-up to the no-show analysis we discussed last week. Customers using Dock Scheduler have asked whether they can see which carriers and time windows miss their booked dock appointments most often. Right now the appointment history records a no-show only when a dock lead marks it manually, so the data is incomplete and inconsistent between sites.

This ticket covers a first version of the report. It does not change how appointments are booked or how no-shows are recorded. It reads existing appointment and check-in events and groups them into patterns.

**Context**

- Appointment events already include booked start, actual check-in, and status. About a third of no-show records have no status set, so the report must infer them from the absence of a check-in event within the booking window plus a grace period.
- The grace period should be configurable per site. We do not have a default yet. Product has suggested starting with 30 minutes but this needs confirmation from Leila Haddad before we ship.
- Predict ETA arrival estimates are not an input to this version. Oskar Thorsby's team has asked us to keep the first cut independent of the ETA models so we can measure the baseline first.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. The report groups no-shows by carrier, site, dock door, and booked hour of day.
2. A no-show is counted when there is no check-in event within the booking window plus the site's grace period, unless the status was set manually to cancelled or rescheduled.
3. Manually set no-show statuses override inferred ones and are labeled as manual in the output.
4. The report runs against at least 90 days of history and completes within the existing reporting timeout.
5. Each row shows the count, the total booked appointments for the same group, and the resulting no-show rate. Groups with fewer than 10 booked appointments are hidden by default.
6. Customer-facing views only show the customer's own carriers and sites. Cross-tenant data must not appear.
7. Unit tests cover the inference rule, the manual override, and the grace-period boundary.

**Out of scope**

- Automatic notifications to carriers
- Changes to the dock booking flow
- Any use of Predict ETA data

---

# Pricing FAQ for Account Teams

**Author:** Theo Wexley, Technical Writer
**Date:** September 21, 2026, 09:00 UTC
**Source:** H2 Pricing and Discount Policy

## Purpose

This FAQ answers common questions from account teams about Northstar list pricing and discount approvals. It is drawn from the H2 pricing and discount policy. If anything here conflicts with that policy, the policy governs.

## Products and list prices

**What are the list prices?**

| Product | List price |
|---|---|
| Northstar Track | $14 per truck per month |
| Predict ETA | $9 per truck per month |
| Dock Scheduler | $6 per truck per month |

**How is pricing counted?**
Pricing is counted per truck per month for each product subscribed. A customer running all three products on 40 trucks pays for 40 trucks on each product.

## Discounts

**Who can approve a discount?**
Discounts up to 25% can be approved by the VP Sales. Anything above 25% goes to the CFO, after the VP Sales signs off.

**Can I offer a discount on one product only?**
Yes. Discounts are applied per product, and the 25% limit applies to each product line separately.

**Where do I record an approved discount?**
Record the approved percentage, the approver's name, and the product in the opportunity record before sending the quote. Revenue Operations checks these fields during deal review.

## Questions not covered here

If a customer asks about a situation this FAQ does not address, contact Revenue Operations before making a commitment. Do not quote terms that are not in the policy.
